A text that describes a picture
A text that summarizes a book
questions.explanation: Argumentativo describes a text that argues: it defends a position, gives reasons and answers objections. A story is narrativo and a description descriptivo. The adjective doesn't describe a quarrelsome person.

questions.stem: How does the lesson present Octavio Paz's idea that Mexicans wear "masks" to protect themselves?
choices: As a scientific finding about Mexican psychology
As something Paz later took back
As a famous but debated generalization
As Vasconcelos's idea, which Paz criticized
questions.explanation: The lesson says the generalizations about "the Mexican" in El laberinto de la soledad are debated now, though the book is still widely read. An essay is a reflection, not a scientific study, so its claims are judged as arguments.

questions.stem: How did Mexican muralism begin?
choices: Private collectors in New York commissioned the first murals in 1910.
Frida Kahlo founded a school of mural painting in 1938.
In 1921 José Vasconcelos, head of the new SEP, invited painters to cover the walls of public buildings.
The painters decided to paint on walls because canvas was too expensive.
questions.explanation: The state, through Vasconcelos and the SEP, was the movement's first great patron, and the former Escuela Nacional Preparatoria (San Ildefonso) its first great site, from 1921–1922. The idea was an art the whole public could see.

questions.stem: Which artist from the lesson was not a muralist and painted mostly small oil paintings, many of them self-portraits?
questions.explanation: Frida Kahlo (1907–1954) began painting after a bus accident in 1925 and worked mostly on small óleos. Rivera, Orozco and Siqueiros are los tres grandes of muralism.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this mural design.

image.alt: An original mural design with five numbered parts: 1 the two volcanoes at the top, 2 the tall woman holding a book in the middle, 3 the factory on the left, 4 the cornfield and farmer on the right, 5 the row of small figures along the bottom.

questions.explanation: The volcanoes are al fondo (in the background), the woman with the book is la figura central, the factory is a la izquierda and the cornfield a la derecha, and the row of readers is en primer plano (in the foreground). The design has no frame (el marco) or signature (la firma).

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
choices: line drawn with a pencil or pen
questions.explanation: El pincel is the tool, la pincelada the mark it leaves, el lienzo the fabric painted on, el trazo a drawn line, and el mecenas the person or institution who pays for art. A picture frame is el marco.

questions.stem: What does it mean to paint a mural "al fresco"?
choices: To paint it outdoors in cool weather
To apply pigment in water to wet plaster, so the color becomes part of the wall
To paint it quickly in oil on a large canvas
To paint it with spray guns and industrial paint
questions.explanation: In fresco the color is absorbed into fresh lime plaster as it dries, which is why only one day's area is plastered at a time. Oil on canvas is óleo sobre lienzo; industrial paints were among Siqueiros's experiments. The adjective fresco (cool, fresh) is a different word.

questions.stem: Complete with the passive of pintar in the preterite: "Muchos murales de la SEP ___ ___ por Diego Rivera entre 1923 y 1928."
questions.explanation: The ser passive is ser + participle, and the participle agrees with the subject: muchos murales fueron pintados. The agent comes with por: por Diego Rivera.

questions.stem: Complete: "Dos coleccionistas fueron los principales ___ de la joven pintora."
questions.explanation: El mecenas is the same in the plural (los mecenas) and for a woman (la mecenas), like el lunes / los lunes. Mecenazgo is patronage, the activity, not the people.

questions.stem: In the model description, "Al fondo se ven dos volcanes y un sol enorme cuyos rayos parecen salir del libro", whose rays are they?
questions.explanation: Cuyo means whose; here its antecedent is the noun just before it, un sol, and it agrees with what is possessed, rayos: cuyos rayos. The rays belong to the sun and seem to come out of the book.

questions.stem: Which of these sentences hedge an interpretation instead of stating a fact? Select all that apply.
choices: El mural parece simbolizar la unión del campo y la ciudad.
La mujer podría representar a una maestra.
Al fondo se ven dos volcanes.
Quizá el sol aluda al conocimiento.
questions.explanation: Parece, podría and quizá (with the subjunctive aluda) present a reading as possible, which is how a careful guide or critic talks about meaning. The date and the volcanoes are facts that anyone can check.

questions.stem: What happened to the mural Diego Rivera painted for the Rockefeller Center in New York in 1933?
choices: It was moved to the Detroit Institute of Arts.
It was bought by the SEP.
His patrons objected to its content and it was destroyed in 1934.
questions.explanation: A patron can also limit an artist: the mural was destroyed in 1934, and Rivera painted a new version at the Palacio de Bellas Artes in Mexico City that same year. His Detroit murals (1932–1933) are a different work.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: It's a portrait whose colors are very bright.
questions.explanation: Cuyo agrees with the thing possessed, colores (masculine plural): cuyos colores. Cuyas would agree with a feminine plural noun. Vivo is A2's word for a bright color.

questions.stem: How many syllables does "óleo" have in careful speech?
questions.explanation: Ó-le-o: in careful speech e and o stay in separate syllables, so the word has three, stressed on the first (that's why it has a written accent).

questions.stem: Which of these is written like a museum label (ficha técnica)?
choices: Este mural me encanta porque tiene colores muy alegres.
La lectura. Ana Ruiz. 1968. Fresco sobre muro, 4 × 9 m.
Ana Ruiz pintó La lectura hace mucho tiempo, creo.
Si vas a Puebla, no te pierdas este mural.
questions.explanation: A label gives title, artist, date, technique and support, size and place, in a fixed order and without verbs. The others are an opinion, a vague memory and a recommendation.

questions.stem: Whose murals in the Hospicio Cabañas in Guadalajara (late 1930s) are part of a UNESCO World Heritage site?
questions.explanation: José Clemente Orozco, born in Zapotlán el Grande, Jalisco, painted the Hospicio Cabañas, a World Heritage site since 1997. Rivera's best-known murals are in the SEP and the Palacio Nacional, and Siqueiros's last great one is at the Polyforum (1971).

questions.stem: According to INALI's catalog (2008), how are Mexico's Indigenous languages counted?
questions.explanation: The catalog has three levels: 11 language families, 68 agrupaciones (what most people call languages: náhuatl, maya, zapoteco…) and 364 variantes. "68 languages" and "364 variants" are both correct at their level.

questions.stem: What does the Ley General de Derechos Lingüísticos de los Pueblos Indígenas (2003) establish?
choices: The Indigenous languages it recognizes and Spanish are national languages with the same validity.
Spanish is the only official language of Mexico.
Indigenous languages may be used only in private life.
questions.explanation: Article 4 makes the recognized Indigenous languages and Spanish lenguas nacionales with the same validity in the places and contexts where they are spoken, article 9 protects their use in public and private life, and article 14 created INALI. The law doesn't oblige every school to teach Nahuatl.

questions.stem: According to INEGI's 2020 census, which language had the second-largest number of speakers aged 3 and over?

image.alt: A horizontal bar chart of speakers aged 3 and over in the 2020 census: náhuatl 1,651,958; maya 774,755; tseltal 589,144; tsotsil 550,274; mixteco 526,593; zapoteco 490,845.

questions.explanation: Maya, with 774,755 speakers, comes after Nahuatl (1,651,958). Nahuatl has more than twice as many speakers as Maya: El náhuatl tiene más del doble de hablantes que el maya.

questions.stem: Complete with the two words for "mother tongue": "Mi ___ ___ es el maya: es la primera lengua que aprendí en casa."
questions.explanation: La lengua materna is the first language you learn at home. La lengua means both language and tongue; in this topic it is more common than el idioma.

questions.stem: Match each word from Nahuatl to its meaning in Mexican Spanish.
questions.explanation: All five are nahuatlismos: papalote from papalotl (butterfly), guajolote from huexolotl, elote from elotl, popote from popotl and tianguis from tianquiztli. A grasshopper is el chapulín, another word from Nahuatl.

questions.stem: Why does the lesson advise against calling Nahuatl or Maya "dialectos"?
choices: Because dialecto is a Spain word not used in Mexico
Because only languages with many speakers can be called dialects
Because it suggests they are not full languages, which is false
Because the law forbids the word
questions.explanation: In linguistics a dialect is a regional variety of one language (Mexican Spanish is a dialect of Spanish). Calling Nahuatl a dialecto implies it isn't a real language, a false idea long used to look down on its speakers. The word itself is normal Spanish, and no law forbids it.

questions.stem: Which sentences are accurate and respectful? Select all that apply.
choices: En ese municipio se habla tsotsil.
En ese pueblo todavía hablan un dialecto.
El zapoteco es una lengua originaria.
Muchos jóvenes de la región son bilingües en mixteco y español.
Los jóvenes ya hablan bien porque hablan español.
questions.explanation: Naming the language, calling it a lengua and describing bilingualism are accurate. Dialecto treats a language as less than one, and "ya hablan bien" implies that speaking an Indigenous language is speaking badly.

questions.stem: Listen to the reporter. How many speakers of Nahuatl does he mention?

audio.text: Según el censo de 2020, el náhuatl tiene más de un millón seiscientos mil hablantes.

questions.explanation: Un millón seiscientos mil = 1,600,000; más de = more than (the census counted 1,651,958 speakers aged 3 and over). Listen for millón, which marks the millions.

questions.stem: Listen to the teacher. Why didn't her parents teach Nahuatl to her younger brothers and sisters?

audio.text: Cuando yo era niña, en la escuela nos regañaban si hablábamos náhuatl. Mis papás decidieron no enseñárselo a mis hermanos menores para que no sufrieran lo mismo.

choices: Because the school didn't offer Nahuatl classes
Because they didn't speak it well themselves
Because the children didn't want to learn it
So that the children wouldn't be scolded and suffer as she had
questions.explanation: Para que no sufrieran lo mismo: so that they wouldn't suffer the same thing she did (being scolded at school for speaking Nahuatl). Para que after a past verb takes the imperfect subjunctive.

questions.stem: Put INALI's three levels in order, from the broadest to the narrowest.
questions.explanation: A family (such as yuto-nahua) contains several groupings (such as náhuatl), and a grouping contains several regional variants. So the counts grow as the levels narrow: 11, 68, 364.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Tsotsil is spoken in that town.
questions.explanation: The passive se agrees with the language, a singular noun: se habla tsotsil. The place phrase can come first or last. Se hablan would need a plural (se hablan tsotsil y español). A language name as subject before the verb needs its article (El tsotsil se habla…), so that order isn't offered here.

questions.stem: In central Mexico, what does "jitomate" usually mean?
questions.explanation: Jitomate (from Nahuatl xitomatl) is the red tomato; in central Mexico tomate often means the green tomatillo. Elsewhere, tomate is the red one.

questions.stem: What do aguacate, tomate and mecate have in common?
choices: They come from Taíno, a Caribbean language.
They come from Nahuatl words ending in -tl, which became -te in Spanish.
They come from Latin through Spain.
They are Spain words that Mexico doesn't use.
questions.explanation: Ahuacatl, tomatl and mecatl lost the -tl ending, hard for Spanish speakers at the end of a word, and became -te. The pattern is a strong clue, not a proof: check a dictionary before stating an etymology.

questions.stem: Which of these words came into Spanish from Taíno, a language of the Caribbean, rather than from Nahuatl or Maya?
questions.explanation: Huracán, like canoa, maíz and hamaca, comes from Taíno, which the Spanish met first, in 1492. Papalote and aguacate are from Nahuatl, and cenote from Maya.

questions.stem: Why is the preterite used in "Vivió veinte años en París"?
choices: It happened before another past event
The twenty years are presented as a closed period
The period reaches up to now
questions.explanation: A period with a measured length that is over (veinte años, toda su vida, de 1990 a 2000) takes the preterite, however long it was. A habit or background would be imperfect (Cuando vivía en París, escribía…); "before another past" is the pluperfect; "up to now" is the present perfect.

questions.stem: Choose the tense: "Cuando yo ___ niña, mi abuela me contaba la misma historia cada domingo."
questions.explanation: Era sets the background (a stage of life), and contaba is a habit: both imperfect. Fui would present childhood as a closed event, he sido reaches up to now, and había sido would place it before another past moment.

questions.stem: A woman from Madrid says: "Hoy he comido con mi madre." What is true?
choices: It is a mistake: she should say "comí"
It means she eats with her mother every day
It means the meal is still going on
It is the usual pattern in most of Spain for something finished today
questions.explanation: In most of Spain the present perfect is the usual tense for today and the very recent past, even for finished events. In Mexico you would more often hear "Hoy comí con mi mamá", but neither is wrong in its region.

questions.stem: What is the usual way to say "I saw your brother this morning" in Mexico?
choices: Esta mañana he visto a tu hermano.
Esta mañana vi a tu hermano.
Esta mañana veía a tu hermano.
Esta mañana había visto a tu hermano.
questions.explanation: In Mexico and most of Latin America the preterite covers anything finished, even this morning. "He visto" is the usual pattern in most of Spain; "veía" would describe something in progress or a habit; "había visto" needs a later past moment.

questions.stem: Which sentence is in the historical present?
choices: En 1936 se mudó a la Ciudad de México.
En 1936 se muda a la Ciudad de México.
En 1936 se mudaba a la Ciudad de México.
En 1936 se había mudado a la Ciudad de México.
questions.explanation: The historical present tells a past event in the present tense (se muda) with a date to place it. The others are the preterite, the imperfect and the pluperfect.

questions.stem: What does "Iba a llamarte, pero se me acabó la batería" mean?
choices: I used to call you, but my battery died.
I went to call you, but my battery died.
I had called you, but my battery died.
I was going to call you, but my battery died.
questions.explanation: Ir (imperfect) a + infinitive tells a plan that was about to happen and didn't, very often followed by "pero". It is not a habit here, and "I went" would be fui.

questions.stem: At a school office you say: "Quería pedirle un favor." What does the imperfect do here?
choices: It makes a request now sound more polite
It says you no longer want the favor
It describes a habit in the past
It says you asked before and were refused
questions.explanation: The polite imperfect places the wish a moment in the past, which softens a request made now: "I wanted to ask you a favor" = I'd like to ask you a favor.

questions.stem: In a life story, which of these are usually told in the preterite? Select all that apply.
choices: A period with a measured length that is over: veinte años en París
A dated event: su boda en 1958
A childhood habit: cada domingo después de misa
questions.explanation: Closed periods and dated events take the preterite (vivió veinte años, se casó en 1958). Habits and the scene are background: imperfect (cada domingo íbamos…, no había carretera).

questions.stem: Complete with the preterite of fallecer: "Mi abuela ___ en 2009."
questions.explanation: Falleció: a dated, finished event takes the preterite in Mexico and in Spain. Fallecer is the formal verb for morir; only its present and present subjunctive are irregular (fallezco, fallezca).

questions.stem: Match each expression to its meaning.
questions.explanation: En aquel entonces = back then (often with the imperfect); a lo largo de = throughout; a raíz de = as a result of, following; desde entonces = since then (B1). "Until then" is hasta entonces.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in the historical present.
questions.prompt: In 1910 the Revolution breaks out.
questions.explanation: "En 1910 estalla la Revolución." The date can come first or last, and the subject can follow the verb, as is common in Spanish. Estalló is the preterite, not the historical present.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: He lived in Paris for twenty years.
questions.explanation: "Vivió veinte años en París": a closed period, so the preterite, however long it lasted. The place or the length can also come first. Vivía would present Paris as background and doesn't fit a measured, finished period.

questions.stem: Elena, in Mexico, has opened her grandmother's box many times, and still does. Complete with abrir (yo): "Desde entonces la ___ muchas veces."
questions.explanation: Repetition up to now takes the present perfect, in Mexico too: he abierto (irregular participle abierto). Abrí would close the period; abría would be a past habit that is over.

questions.stem: Your classmate's thesis was due yesterday. You say: "Espero que ___ la tesis."
questions.explanation: Esperar que takes the subjunctive; the main verb is present and the event is already over, so the perfect subjunctive: hayas entregado. Has entregado and entregaste are indicative; hubieras entregado follows a past main verb (Esperaba que…).

questions.stem: What does "No creo que haya estudiado" mean?
choices: I didn't think he had studied.
questions.explanation: Haya estudiado points to before now. "He'll study" and "he's studying" would be the present subjunctive (No creo que estudie); "I didn't think he had studied" has a past main verb (No creía que hubiera estudiado).

questions.stem: Complete: "Te llamo en cuanto ___ el resultado."
questions.explanation: After en cuanto about the future, Spanish uses the subjunctive: salga, or haya salido to stress "once it is out". Ha salido and había salido are indicative, and the future (habrá salido) is not used after en cuanto.

questions.stem: Complete: "Es el mejor curso que ___." Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: After a superlative both moods are correct: que he tomado (indicative) and que haya tomado (subjunctive, a little more emphatic). Tomaba is an imperfect habit, and hubiera tomado would need a past or conditional main verb.

questions.stem: In Mexico, what lets a graduate practice a profession such as medicine?
questions.explanation: The cédula profesional, issued by the SEP's Dirección General de Profesiones, is the license to practice. The examen profesional is the thesis defense, the plan de estudios the curriculum, and the colegiatura is tuition.

questions.stem: What does "Egresó en 2024, pero se tituló en 2026" mean?
choices: She enrolled in 2024 and finished in 2026.
She finished her courses in 2024 and got her degree in 2026.
She failed in 2024 and passed in 2026.
She got her degree in 2024 and a master's in 2026.
questions.explanation: In Mexico egresar means finishing the coursework; titularse means completing every requirement (thesis or another option, social service) and receiving the degree, which can come years later.

questions.stem: Complete with the perfect subjunctive of hacer (él / ella): "Busco a alguien que ___ un posgrado en el extranjero."
questions.explanation: The person may not exist, so the relative clause takes the subjunctive, and the description is about the past: haya hecho (irregular participle hecho).

questions.stem: Complete with the perfect subjunctive of volver (ellos): "Es raro que todavía no ___."
questions.explanation: Es raro que is a value judgment, so the subjunctive; the main verb is present and the not-returning reaches up to now: hayan vuelto (irregular participle vuelto).

questions.stem: Put the steps of a typical degree at a Mexican public university in order.
choices: cursar las materias y juntar créditos
questions.explanation: First the entrance exam, then the courses and credits, then you finish your coursework (egresar); the thesis defense (examen profesional) completes the degree, and only with the degree can you apply for the cédula profesional.

questions.stem: Label the numbered places on the campus.

image.alt: A university campus seen from above with six numbered places: a tall building with a clock and a flag, a building with an open book on its front, a long building with columns, a classroom with a board and desks, a small building with a steaming cup, and a parking lot with cars.

questions.explanation: The clock tower with the flag is the rectoría (the president's office); the book marks the biblioteca; the building with columns is a facultad; the board and desks are an aula (A1's salón de clases); the cup is the cafetería; the cars are the estacionamiento.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: El asesor (la asesora) guides your thesis; la colegiatura is tuition (Mexico); el promedio is your average; el plagio is plagiarism. Enrollment is la matrícula.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I hope you've rested.
questions.explanation: "Espero que hayas descansado." Esperar que takes the subjunctive, and the resting is already done, so haya + participle. Has is the indicative and can't follow esperar que.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I don't know anyone who has failed that exam.
questions.explanation: "No conozco a nadie que haya reprobado ese examen." A relative clause about someone who doesn't exist (a nadie) takes the subjunctive; the event is past, so haya reprobado.

questions.stem: Which form makes it clear that the not-inviting came first? "Me dolió que no me ___ a la reunión."
questions.explanation: After a past main verb (me dolió), an earlier event takes the pluperfect subjunctive. Has invitado and habías invitado are indicative; habrías invitado is the conditional perfect. (Que no me invitaras is also common when the order is obvious; que no me hayas invitado is heard in Latin American speech but breaks the usual sequence of tenses.)

questions.stem: You told your brother a secret and now regret it. Complete: "Ojalá no le ___ nada."
questions.explanation: A regret about the past: ojalá + pluperfect subjunctive. Ojalá never takes the conditional or the indicative. "Ojalá no le haya dicho nada" is correct Spanish but means "I hope she hasn't told him", a hope about something you don't know.

questions.stem: Complete: "Me saludó como si no ___ nada."
questions.explanation: Como si always takes a past subjunctive. The argument came before the greeting, so the pluperfect subjunctive: hubiera pasado. The present or perfect subjunctive and the conditional are never used after como si.

questions.stem: Complete: "Me habla como si ___ mi jefe."
questions.explanation: Como si + imperfect subjunctive for something at the same time as the main verb, even when the main verb is present: como si fuera (or fuese) mi jefe.

questions.stem: Is "No creo que lo dijera ayer" correct?
choices: No: after "no creo" it must be "dijo"
Yes: a present main verb can take a past subjunctive for a past event
No: after a present main verb it must be "haya dicho"
questions.explanation: The sequence-of-tenses table is a strong default, not a law. With a dated past event, a present main verb can take the imperfect subjunctive; "No creo que lo haya dicho" is also fine. Negated creer takes the subjunctive.

questions.stem: What does "Mi mejor amigo me decepcionó" mean?
choices: My best friend cheated on me.
questions.explanation: Decepcionar is a false friend: it means "to disappoint". To deceive is engañar, to betray is traicionar, and "to cheat on" a partner is also engañar.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct standard Spanish? Select all that apply.
choices: Me molestó que no me hubieras llamado.
Me molestó que no me llamaras.
Ojalá no le habría dicho nada.
Me saludó como si no haya pasado nada.
No podía creer que me hubiera mentido.
questions.explanation: After a past main verb, the pluperfect subjunctive (hubieras llamado, hubiera mentido) or, when the order is obvious, the imperfect subjunctive (llamaras) are both correct. Ojalá never takes the conditional (hubiera dicho), and como si never takes the perfect subjunctive (hubiera pasado).

questions.stem: Complete with the pluperfect subjunctive of decir (tú): "Me habría gustado que me lo ___."
questions.explanation: A conditional main verb (me habría gustado) and an earlier event: hubieras dicho (or hubieses dicho). The participle of decir is dicho.

questions.stem: Complete with the pluperfect subjunctive of conocer (nosotros): "Actúa como si nunca nos ___."
questions.explanation: Como si + an event before the main verb: pluperfect subjunctive. The nosotros form carries an accent: hubiéramos (or hubiésemos) conocido.

questions.stem: Match each verb to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Traicionar = to betray; engañar = to deceive (or to cheat on); decepcionar = to disappoint; reencontrarse = to meet again; distanciarse = to drift apart. "To forgive" is A2's perdonar.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I wish I hadn't told him anything.
questions.explanation: "Ojalá no le hubiera dicho nada." A regret about the past: ojalá + pluperfect subjunctive, with no and the pronoun before hubiera. The conditional never follows ojalá.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: It hurt me that you hadn't invited me.
questions.explanation: "Me dolió que no me hubieras invitado." A past main verb and an earlier event: pluperfect subjunctive. The que clause can also come first: "Que no me hubieras invitado me dolió." Habrías invitado is the conditional perfect, which a feeling verb like doler doesn't take in its que clause.

questions.stem: Pablo never forgets a wrong; he holds grudges by nature. Which sentence says that?
questions.explanation: Ser rencoroso describes a trait: someone who holds grudges. Estar dolido is being hurt now, ser leal is being loyal, and tener celos is being jealous.

questions.stem: Complete: "Si ___ antes, no habría perdido el vuelo."
questions.explanation: A past condition: si + pluperfect subjunctive (hubiera or hubiese salido). After si meaning "if", standard Spanish uses neither the conditional (habría) nor the present or perfect subjunctive; había salido is indicative and doesn't express an unreal past.

questions.stem: Complete: "Si hubiera estudiado medicina, ahora ___ médica."
questions.explanation: A past condition with a present result (ahora): the simple conditional, sería. Habría sido would be a past result; fuera is subjunctive and belongs in the si clause; será is a real future.

questions.stem: Raúl is always careless. Complete: "Si fuera más prudente, no ___ el accidente el sábado."
questions.explanation: A lasting condition (he is careless in general: si fuera) with a past result (el sábado): conditional perfect, habría tenido (hubiera tenido is also heard). Tendría would be a present or future result; había tenido is indicative; tuviera belongs in the si clause.

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT standard Spanish?
choices: Si hubiera sabido, no habría venido.
Si habría sabido, no habría venido.
Si hubiera sabido, no hubiera venido.
De haberlo sabido, no habría venido.
questions.explanation: After si meaning "if", standard Spanish doesn't use the conditional; it is heard in some regions in casual speech. The other three are correct: hubiera in the result is accepted by the Nueva gramática, and de + compound infinitive replaces the si clause.

questions.stem: What does "De no haber sido por ti, me habría perdido" mean?
choices: Since it wasn't you, I got lost.
If it hadn't been for you, I would have gotten lost.
If you hadn't gotten lost, I wouldn't have either.
Because of you, I got lost.
questions.explanation: De no haber sido por + noun or pronoun = if it hadn't been for. The result is the conditional perfect: me habría perdido, "I would have gotten lost" (but didn't, thanks to you).

questions.stem: Which si clause means the same as "De haberlo sabido…"?
questions.explanation: De + haber + participle is a past condition: = si + pluperfect subjunctive. Si lo supiera is about now; si lo sabía is a real past condition; si lo habría sabido isn't standard.

questions.stem: Which sentences mean "If you had told me, I would have helped you"? Select all that apply.
choices: Si me lo hubieras dicho, te habría ayudado.
Te habría ayudado si me lo hubieras dicho.
Si me lo hubieras dicho, te hubiera ayudado.
Si me lo habrías dicho, te habría ayudado.
Si me lo dijeras, te ayudaría.
questions.explanation: Either clause can come first, and hubiera can replace habría in the result. Si + conditional (habrías dicho) isn't standard, and si me lo dijeras, te ayudaría is about now or the future, not the past.

questions.stem: Complete with the conditional perfect of evitar (tú): "Si hubieras revisado las llantas, ___ el accidente."
questions.explanation: The result of a past condition: habría, habrías… + participle: habrías evitado. (In speech you'll also hear hubieras evitado; the question asks for the conditional perfect.)

questions.stem: Complete with the participle of prever: "Nadie había ___ la tormenta."
questions.explanation: Prever is conjugated like ver, so its participle is irregular: previsto (like visto). There is no verb "preveer".

questions.stem: Match each kind of condition to its example.
choices: Si hubiera salido antes, no habría perdido el vuelo.
Si hubiera estudiado medicina, ahora sería médica.
questions.explanation: Real: si + present. Hypothetical now: si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional. Past: si + pluperfect subjunctive + conditional perfect. Mixed: si + pluperfect subjunctive + conditional (ahora). Si habría sabido isn't standard.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: If I had left earlier, I wouldn't have missed the flight.
questions.explanation: "Si hubiera salido antes, no habría perdido el vuelo." Either clause can come first; write a comma after the si clause when it comes first. After si meaning "if", never the conditional (habría salido).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: If it hadn't been for you, I would have gotten lost.
questions.explanation: "De no haber sido por ti, me habría perdido." The phrase can also come second: "Me habría perdido de no haber sido por ti." In speech, "si no hubiera sido por ti" is also common.

questions.stem: What does "Mudarnos al centro fue un acierto" mean?
choices: Moving downtown was a good choice.
Moving downtown was a stroke of luck.
questions.explanation: Un acierto is a good choice or the right decision (from acertar, to get it right). A stroke of luck is un golpe de suerte, and a mishap is un imprevisto.

questions.stem: How does a typical Mexican esquela announce a death?
choices: Tenemos la noticia de que murió…
questions.explanation: The esquela uses fixed, formal wording with the death as a noun: el sensible fallecimiento (sensible = sad, regrettable). "Les cuento que se murió" is conversational, and "se fue al otro mundo" is a flippant euphemism.

questions.stem: In an esquela, "Sus restos serán velados en Capillas San José" tells you where…
questions.explanation: Velar = to keep vigil: the remains will lie at that funeral home for el velorio. The burial is el sepelio.

questions.stem: What is "el sepelio"?
questions.explanation: El sepelio is the formal word for the burial (el entierro in everyday speech). The wake is el velorio, mourning is el luto, and the headstone is la lápida.

questions.stem: According to the lesson, what is el novenario in Catholic families?
choices: The ninth anniversary of a death
Nine days of prayers after the death, often ending with a Mass
questions.explanation: El novenario: nine days of prayers, usually including the rosary, after a death; a Mass is often celebrated when it ends. Customs vary by region and family.

questions.stem: Which expression means "to wear black for mourning"?
questions.explanation: Vestirse de luto: el luto is the outward signs and period of mourning. Vivir el duelo is going through grief; rendir homenaje is paying tribute; dar el pésame is offering condolences.

questions.stem: In the obituary of Teresa Ochoa, why is it "solía decir" and not "solió decir"?
choices: It describes something she used to say habitually
It is more formal than the preterite
It happened before another past event
The obituary is in the historical present
questions.explanation: Soler + infinitive expresses a habit, and a past habit is told in the imperfect: solía decir (she used to say). "It happened before" would be the pluperfect, and the obituary is told in the preterite, not the historical present.

questions.stem: How does a newspaper obituary usually begin, as the lesson describes it?
choices: With the news: who died, when, where and at what age
With the arrangements for the wake
With a prayer for the dead person
questions.explanation: An obituary is journalism: it starts with the news (Falleció ayer en…, a los 84 años, la arquitecta…), then tells the life and ends with the legacy. Arrangements and the family's names belong to the esquela.

questions.stem: What is "una obra póstuma"?
choices: the last work an author wrote
a work published after its author's death
a work in honor of someone who died
questions.explanation: Póstumo means after death: una obra póstuma is published after the author dies. A work in honor of someone is un homenaje; it can be posthumous (un homenaje póstumo) if given after death.

questions.stem: Why does the Lola Beltrán summary say "algunas fuentes dicen 1932"?
choices: She was born on New Year's Eve
The writer isn't sure who she was
Sources disagree on her birth year, and a careful summary says so
questions.explanation: EFE gives March 7, 1931, but some reference works give 1932. Hedges like algunas fuentes dicen, según EFE and al menos are part of a well-made obituary.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this esquela.

image.alt: A newspaper death notice in a black border with five numbered parts: the opening lines Con profundo pesar comunicamos el sensible fallecimiento de la señora; the name Rosa María Treviño Garza (1938–2026); the line Sus hijos Jorge y Elena, sus nietos y demás familiares; a line beginning Velorio; and a line beginning Sepelio.

questions.explanation: An esquela opens with a formula (Con profundo pesar…), names the deceased with a title, lists the family, and gives the arrangements: the velorio (wake) and the sepelio (burial). It doesn't tell the life story or, usually, the cause of death.

questions.stem: Match each genre to its description.
choices: a short paid notice with fixed formulas
questions.explanation: The family or colleagues pay for an esquela; the newspaper writes a necrológica (obituario); a relative or colleague speaks the palabras de despedida; the novenario is a custom, not a text. A will is un testamento.

questions.stem: Complete with the future of rendir: "El próximo sábado, la colonia le ___ homenaje a la maestra."
questions.explanation: Rendir changes its stem in the present (rindo) and preterite (rindió), but the future is regular: rendirá. Rendir homenaje a alguien = to pay tribute to someone.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'm glad that so many of you have come.
questions.explanation: "Me alegra que tantos de ustedes hayan venido." A feeling about something already done: present main verb + perfect subjunctive. The subject can also follow the verb ("…que hayan venido tantos de ustedes"), and the que clause can come first ("Que tantos de ustedes hayan venido me alegra").

questions.stem: What is the modern equivalent of "Apenas hubo terminado la misa, salieron a la plaza"?
choices: Apenas termine la misa, salieron a la plaza.
Apenas terminaría la misa, salieron a la plaza.
Apenas terminó la misa, salieron a la plaza.
Apenas terminaba la misa, salieron a la plaza.
questions.explanation: The pretérito anterior (hubo terminado) marks an action finished just before another; modern Spanish uses the preterite: apenas terminó. The subjunctive would refer to the future, and the conditional and imperfect change the meaning.

questions.stem: In a novel: "Vivía en la casa que construyera su abuelo." What does "construyera" mean here?
questions.explanation: In literary style the -ra form can keep its old meaning of a pluperfect indicative: que construyera = que había construido. Nothing here triggers a subjunctive.

questions.stem: Which phrase is the modern equivalent of "sea cual fuere"?
questions.explanation: Fuere is the future subjunctive of ser; modern Spanish uses the present subjunctive: sea cual sea (whatever it may be), plural sean cuales sean.

questions.stem: How is the future subjunctive formed?
choices: From the ellos preterite: drop -ron and add -re, -res, -re…
From the yo present: drop -o and add -ere
questions.explanation: Like the imperfect subjunctive, it comes from the ellos preterite: tuvieron → tuvie- → tuviere; fueron → fuere; hubieron → hubiere.

questions.stem: What does "No bien hubieron llegado, empezó a llover" mean?
choices: They didn't arrive well, and it started to rain.
No sooner had they arrived than it started to rain.
They hadn't arrived yet when it started to rain.
If they had arrived, it would have rained.
questions.explanation: No bien (literary) = no sooner, as soon as; hubieron llegado is the pretérito anterior. Modern: En cuanto llegaron, empezó a llover.

questions.stem: According to the lesson, which is true of Bernal Díaz del Castillo's Historia verdadera?
choices: He wrote it as letters to Charles V between 1519 and 1526.
It was printed in Guatemala while he was alive.
It is a historical novel written in the twentieth century.
He probably finished it around 1568, and it was first printed in Madrid in 1632.
questions.explanation: Bernal wrote it in old age in Guatemala and probably finished it around 1568; the manuscript was first printed in Madrid in 1632. The letters to Charles V (1519–1526) are Hernán Cortés's Cartas de relación.

questions.stem: In the clause "El arrendatario que no pagare la renta… deberá cubrir un recargo", why "pagare"?
choices: Old legal style uses the future subjunctive for possible future cases
It is a spelling mistake for "pagara"
It is the future indicative of pagar
Legal texts always use the imperfect subjunctive
questions.explanation: Pagare is the future subjunctive: it describes a possible future case, in the old style that some legal writing keeps. Modern equivalent: el arrendatario que no pague.

questions.stem: Which is the future subjunctive of tener (él)?
questions.explanation: Tuvieron → tuvie- + -re = tuviere. Tuviera is the imperfect subjunctive, tendrá the future indicative and tenga the present subjunctive.

questions.stem: Which sentences contain a form you should recognize but not produce in modern Spanish? Select all that apply.
choices: Apenas hubo llegado, se sentó a comer.
Vivía en la casa que construyera su abuelo.
Sea cual fuere la causa, se pagará el recargo.
Ojalá hubieras venido a la fiesta.
Si hubiera sabido, te habría avisado.
questions.explanation: Hubo llegado (pretérito anterior), construyera with pluperfect meaning and fuere (future subjunctive) are literary or legal. Hubieras venido and hubiera sabido are the everyday pluperfect subjunctive from lessons 03 and 04.

questions.stem: Match each literary or legal form to its modern equivalent.
left: la casa que construyera su abuelo
choices: la casa que había construido su abuelo
la casa que construiría su abuelo
questions.explanation: Pretérito anterior → preterite; literary -ra → pluperfect indicative; future subjunctive → present subjunctive. Construiría (conditional) means "would build", a different idea.

questions.stem: Write the modern, everyday version of the formula "sea cual fuere".
questions.explanation: Sea cual sea (whatever it may be): the present subjunctive replaces the old future subjunctive fuere. In the plural: sean cuales sean.

questions.stem: Put the steps for forming the future subjunctive of tener in order.
questions.explanation: Tuvieron → tuvie- → tuviere, the same path as the imperfect subjunctive (tuviera), with -re in place of -ra.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in modern Spanish.
questions.prompt: Whatever the reasons may be, we're going to support you.
questions.explanation: "Sean cuales sean las razones, te vamos a apoyar." With a plural noun the formula agrees: sean cuales sean. It can also come after the main clause.

questions.stem: Complete: "Es injusto que los trabajadores ___ tan poco."
questions.explanation: "Es injusto que" is a value judgment, so the verb after it goes into the subjunctive even though everyone knows the workers earn little: "ganen". The indicative "ganan" and "van a ganar" treat it as information; the infinitive "ganar" would need no "que" and no particular subject ("Es injusto ganar tan poco").

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Creo que la moda rápida es un derroche.
Creo que la moda rápida sea un derroche.
No creo que la moda rápida es un derroche.
Me parece lógico que la moda rápida es un derroche.
questions.explanation: An affirmative opinion ("creo que") presents the idea as true: indicative "es". Negated, it takes the subjunctive ("No creo que… sea"), and a value judgment like "me parece lógico que" also takes the subjunctive ("sea").

questions.stem: Complete: "No sabes lo ___ que son estas botas."
questions.explanation: In "lo + adjective + que" (how …), "lo" never changes but the adjective agrees with the noun it describes: "las botas" is feminine plural, so "lo caras que son". "Lo caro" is the plain neuter pattern ("lo caro es…", the expensive thing).

questions.stem: Complete: "No es que no me guste la moda, ___ no tengo dinero."
questions.explanation: "No es que" + subjunctive rejects an explanation, and "sino que" + indicative gives the real one. Before a full clause with its own verb ("no tengo dinero") the word is "sino que"; plain "sino" goes before a word or phrase ("No es caro, sino justo"). "Si no" (two words) means "if not".

questions.stem: In the radio call-in, why doesn't Ernesto buy secondhand clothes?
choices: He thinks it's too expensive at the street market.
It's not that he's against it; he just doesn't trust it.
He only buys brand-name clothes to look good.
He is a minimalist and doesn't buy clothes at all.
questions.explanation: Ernesto says "No es que esté en contra, sino que no me da confianza": it's not that he's against it; it's that he doesn't trust it. He criticizes people who buy brands "para aparentar"; the minimalist is Sofía, and Daniela is the one who finds it cheap.

questions.stem: What does Sofía say was the hardest part of becoming a minimalist?
questions.explanation: "Lo difícil fue prescindir de las compras por impulso": the hard part was doing without impulse buying. "Prescindir de" = to do without. She now has thirty garments; she didn't throw thirty away.

questions.stem: Complete with the present subjunctive of "tirar": "Me parece absurdo que la gente ___ ropa casi nueva."
questions.explanation: "Me parece absurdo que" is a value judgment ("me parece" + an adjective + "que"), so the verb goes into the subjunctive: "tire" (the person is "la gente", singular). Compare the plain opinion "Me parece que la gente tira mucha ropa", with the indicative.

questions.stem: Complete with the right form of "ser": "No es que yo ___ tacaño, sino que prefiero ahorrar."
questions.explanation: "No es que" denies an explanation, so it takes the subjunctive: "No es que yo sea tacaño". The real reason after "sino que" is asserted, with the indicative: "prefiero".

questions.stem: Match each expression with the mood of the verb that follows it.
questions.explanation: Opinions and certainty ("creo que", "es evidente que") and "lo bueno es que" presenting a fact take the indicative. A value judgment ("es lógico que"), a negated opinion ("no me parece que") and "no es que" take the subjunctive.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Es comprensible que no quieras gastar tanto.
Es absurdo gastar tanto en ropa.
Que la ropa sea desechable me parece absurdo.
Me parece normal que la gente compra de segunda mano.
Me sorprende lo rápido que cambia la moda.
questions.explanation: A value judgment takes the subjunctive ("Es comprensible que no quieras"), or the infinitive when no one in particular is meant ("Es absurdo gastar"). A "que" clause at the start takes the subjunctive ("Que la ropa sea desechable…"). "Lo rápido que cambia" is "how fast it changes", with the indicative. "Me parece normal que" is a judgment, so it needs "compre", not "compra".

questions.stem: Name the numbered items in this closet of secondhand clothes.

image.alt: A wooden closet with open doors: folded jeans and a sign on the shelf; a dress, a jacket with buttons, a T-shirt and a sweater on the rail; a belt on a hook on the left door; sneakers on the floor. Six numbers mark the dress, the jacket, the T-shirt, the jeans, the belt and the sneakers.

questions.explanation: From left to right on the rail: the dress (el vestido), the jacket with buttons (la chamarra) and the T-shirt (la playera, Mexico); the jeans (los jeans) are folded on the shelf, the belt (el cinturón) hangs on the door and the sneakers (los tenis) are on the floor. There is no scarf or hat in the closet; the fourth garment on the rail, not numbered, is a sweater.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: It's logical that cheap clothes don't last long.
questions.explanation: "Es lógico que" is a value judgment, so "durar" goes into the subjunctive, "dure", even though it's a fact. The subject can come before or after the verb ("que la ropa barata dure poco" / "que dure poco la ropa barata"), and the "que" clause can open the sentence: "Que la ropa barata dure poco es lógico". "Dura" (indicative) is wrong in every order.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: You have no idea how expensive the sneakers are.
questions.explanation: "How expensive" is "lo + adjective + que": "lo caros que son los tenis". "Lo" stays the same, but the adjective agrees with "los tenis" (masculine plural): "caros", not "caro". The verb after this "que" is indicative.

questions.stem: Complete: "Me molestaba que mi roomie ___ los trastes sucios."
questions.explanation: The feeling verb is in the past (imperfect "me molestaba"), so the verb after "que" goes into the imperfect subjunctive: "dejara" (or "dejase"). The present subjunctive "deje" goes with a present main verb ("Me molesta que deje…"), and the indicative "dejaba" is wrong after a feeling verb.

questions.stem: Complete: "Me sentó mal que no me ___ a la fiesta."
questions.explanation: "Me sentó mal" (preterite) is a past reaction, so the following verb is in the imperfect subjunctive: "invitaran" (they didn't invite me). "Inviten" would need a present main verb; "invitan" is indicative; "invitar" has no subject.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tus amigos me ___ muy bien."
questions.explanation: "Caer bien" works like "gustar": the people you like are the subject, so the verb agrees with "tus amigos": "me caen bien". "Me cae bien" is for one person; "caigo" and "caes" make "I" or "you" the one who is likable.

questions.stem: A Mexican friend says about a neighbor: "No sé por qué, pero me cae gorda." What does she mean?
choices: She thinks the neighbor has put on weight.
She finds the neighbor very likable.
She can't stand the neighbor, even without a clear reason.
questions.explanation: "Caer gordo" is colloquial for disliking someone strongly, stronger than "caer mal"; it says nothing about weight. "Gorda" agrees with the neighbor, a woman. The opposite would be "me cae bien".

questions.stem: Complete: "Normalmente Memo es tranquilo, pero hoy ___ insoportable."
questions.explanation: "Ser" + adjective describes character ("Memo es tranquilo"); "estar" + adjective describes how someone is behaving now, often unlike their usual self: "hoy está insoportable".

questions.stem: Complete: "Lucía es de las que ___ un vaso a las tres de la mañana."
questions.explanation: After "es de los / las que" the verb is indicative (it describes a real type of person) and usually plural, agreeing with "las que": "lavan". The DPD prefers this plural and admits the singular "lava". A first- or second-person verb ("lavo", "lavas") is wrong, and the subjunctive "laven" doesn't fit a real description.

questions.stem: In the group chat "Depa 302", what starts the discussion?
choices: Loud music after eleven at night.
The dog sleeping in Lucía's bed.
A pot of beans left on the stove since Friday.
questions.explanation: Lucía asks "¿Quién dejó la olla con frijoles en la estufa desde el viernes?" The dog sleeping on the couch and the trash are complaints that come later; the music and the yogurt are on the fridge notes, not in the chat.

questions.stem: According to the house pact, when does the person who cooked not have to wash the dishes?
choices: As long as they leave the kitchen tidy.
Only if the dog is on its blanket.
questions.explanation: Rule 2: "Quien cocina no lava los trastes, siempre que deje la cocina en orden." "Siempre que" + subjunctive = as long as. "A menos que haya fiesta" belongs to the music rule.

questions.stem: Complete with the right form of "poner": "No soportaba que mis vecinos ___ la música a todo volumen."
questions.explanation: "No soportaba" is a past feeling, so the verb after "que" is in the imperfect subjunctive, made from the preterite "pusieron": "pusieran" (or "pusiesen"). Not "ponían" (indicative) or "pongan" (present).

questions.stem: Complete. You are the one who's late: "No soporto ___ tarde."
questions.explanation: When the person who feels and the person who acts are the same, Spanish uses the infinitive: "No soporto llegar tarde". "No soporto que llegues tarde" would mean someone else is late.

questions.stem: Match each phrase with its meaning.
choices: to go down badly, to upset
questions.explanation: "Caer bien", "sentar mal", "hacer gracia" and "caer gordo" all work like "gustar" ("Me cae bien", "Me sentó mal que…", "Me hace gracia", "Me cae gordo"). "Ceder" is an ordinary verb: "Al final cedí". "To put up with" is "soportar" or B1's "aguantar".

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Me molestó que no me avisaras.
Me molesta que no me hayas avisado.
Me molestaba que no me avisas.
No soporto que yo llegue tarde.
questions.explanation: A past feeling takes the imperfect subjunctive ("me molestó que no me avisaras"); a present one takes the present or perfect subjunctive ("me molesta que no me hayas avisado"). "Me molestaba que no me avisas" mixes a past feeling with an indicative present. With the same subject, use the infinitive: "No soporto llegar tarde". "Me caen bien tus primos" agrees with "tus primos".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: It upset her that nobody thanked her.
questions.explanation: "Sentar mal" works like "gustar": "le sentó mal que…". It is a past reaction, so "dar" goes into the imperfect subjunctive: "le diera las gracias". The "que" clause can also come first: "Que nadie le diera las gracias le sentó mal". "Le daba" (indicative) is wrong after a feeling.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'm one of those people who think you have to give in a little.
questions.explanation: After "soy de los que" the verb agrees with "los que", in the third person plural: "piensan". The DPD (concordancia, 4.12) prefers this form and says a first-person verb ("soy de los que pienso") should be avoided. "Hay que ceder un poco" = you have to give in a little.

questions.stem: What does "Aunque lloviera, saldríamos" mean?
choices: Although it was raining, we went out.
Even if it rains, we'll go out.
Even if it had rained, we would have gone out.
Even if it rained (unlikely), we would go out.
questions.explanation: "Aunque" + imperfect subjunctive presents the obstacle as unlikely or imaginary, with a conditional in the main clause: "Even if it rained, we would go out". "Aunque llovía, salimos" is a real past fact; "Aunque llueva, saldremos" a real possibility; "Aunque hubiera llovido, habríamos salido" an imaginary past.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Even if it had rained, we would have climbed"?
questions.explanation: An imaginary past takes the pluperfect subjunctive after "aunque" and the conditional perfect (or "hubiera") in the main clause: "Aunque hubiera llovido, habríamos subido". "Aunque llovía, subimos" says it really rained and they climbed.

questions.stem: Complete: "Si bien el curso ___ caro, incluye todo el equipo."
questions.explanation: "Si bien" (although, formal) concedes a fact and takes the indicative: "Si bien el curso es caro…". Remember that this "si" doesn't mean "if", so it doesn't follow the rules of conditions.

questions.stem: Which connector is typical of speech and is added after the main clause, as an afterthought?
questions.explanation: "Y eso que" + indicative is spoken and comes last: "No se cansó, y eso que subió cinco horas". "Si bien", "pese a que" and "aun cuando" are formal and can open the sentence.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ sabiéndolo, fue."
questions.explanation: "Aun" + gerund means "even + -ing": "Aun sabiéndolo" (even knowing it). Without an accent, "aun" means "even"; "aún" with an accent means "still, yet". "Aunque" needs a conjugated verb ("aunque lo sabía"), and "aun así" stands alone ("Lo sabía; aun así, fue").

questions.stem: In the interview, what does Itzel say about fear?
choices: It doesn't go away, however much experience you have.
questions.explanation: "Por más experiencia que tengas, el miedo no desaparece": no matter how much experience you have, fear doesn't go away. She even says she's afraid of heights herself ("tengo vértigo, y eso que escalo desde los quince años").

questions.stem: According to Itzel, who worries her more?
questions.explanation: "¿Y los temerarios? —Me preocupan más que los cobardes." "Temerario" means reckless. She adds she wouldn't take anyone up without a helmet, even for a lot of money.

questions.stem: Complete with "intentar" (yo): "Por más que lo ___, no puedo mirar hacia abajo."
questions.explanation: "Por más que" usually takes the subjunctive: "Por más que lo intente" (however hard I try). The indicative "intento" is also correct when you present it as a real, repeated fact (I keep trying, and it doesn't work).

questions.stem: Complete with the spoken three-word connector that means "even though" and comes after the main clause: "No se cansó nada, ___ subió cinco horas."
questions.explanation: "Y eso que" + indicative adds a surprising fact after the main clause: "No se cansó nada, y eso que subió cinco horas" (he wasn't tired at all, even though he climbed for five hours). "Aunque" would also fit the meaning, but it is one word and works in every register.

questions.stem: Match each connector with its description.
questions.explanation: "Si bien" is formal and written, with the indicative; "y eso que" is spoken and follows the main clause; "pese a" is the formal twin of "a pesar de"; "aun" + gerund means "even + -ing" ("aun sabiéndolo"); "por más que" means "no matter how much".

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this climbing scene.

image.alt: A climber on a rock wall with a helmet and a harness; a rope runs from her harness up to an anchor and down to a woman standing at the bottom. A flag marks the summit; to the right the wall drops sheer to a valley. Six numbers: the summit, the helmet, the harness, the rope, the drop at the right, and the woman at the bottom.

questions.explanation: The flag marks the summit (la cima); the climber wears a helmet (el casco, B1) and a harness (el arnés), tied to the rope (la cuerda) that the instructor (la instructora) holds from below; the sheer drop on the right is the cliff edge (el precipicio). No backpack or parachute appears.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: However tired she was, she never took off her harness.
questions.explanation: "Por muy" + adjective + "que" usually takes the subjunctive; in the past, the imperfect subjunctive "estuviera". The adjective agrees with the woman: "cansada", not "cansado". The concessive part can come first or last: "Nunca se quitaba el arnés, por muy cansada que estuviera."

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Despite the bad weather, the expedition carried on.
questions.explanation: "Pese a" (formal "a pesar de") + "el" contracts to "pese al mal tiempo"; "pese el" is wrong. The "pese al" phrase can open the sentence, close it, or sit after the subject, and the subject can follow the verb: "La expedición siguió adelante pese al mal tiempo", "Pese al mal tiempo, siguió adelante la expedición". ("La expedición" = the expedition, lesson 08.)

questions.stem: Rodrigo isn't answering his phone. Make a guess: "___ el vuelo."
questions.explanation: A guess about something that has probably just happened takes the future perfect: "Habrá perdido el vuelo" (He must have missed the flight). "Perderá" is a future (he will miss it), "habría perdido" a conditional perfect (he would have missed it), and "había perdido" a plain pluperfect.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "It must have been about three when we arrived"?
questions.explanation: A guess about the past uses the conditional of probability: "Serían las tres". "Eran las tres" states it as a fact. "Serán" guesses about now, so it clashes with "llegamos". Time of day takes the imperfect, not "fueron".

questions.stem: In careful Spanish, which sentence expresses an obligation, not a guess?
choices: Deben de haber cerrado la carretera.
questions.explanation: The recommended distinction is "deber" + infinitive for obligation and "deber de" + infinitive for a guess. The three "deber de" sentences are guesses. (In speech "deber" alone is also used for guesses, and the Nueva gramática accepts it.)

questions.stem: Complete: "A lo mejor ___ en la fila de migración."
questions.explanation: "A lo mejor" (maybe) takes the indicative: "A lo mejor está en la fila". "Quizás" and "tal vez" allow either mood, but "a lo mejor" doesn't.

questions.stem: In the phone call, why does Toño think Rodrigo didn't miss his connection in Bogotá?
choices: Because if he had missed it, he would have told them.
Because the board says the flight is on time.
Because the plane from Lima has no stopover.
questions.explanation: Toño says "Si la hubiera perdido, nos habría avisado": if he had missed it, he would have let them know. That's a past condition from lesson 04. The plane landed an hour earlier, so Rodrigo is probably inside.

questions.stem: Look at the departures board. Which guess fits it?

image.alt: An airport departures board, Salidas, with columns Hora, Destino, Vuelo, Estado: 14:05 Bogotá 712 Retrasado 15:30; 14:20 Cancún 1204 Abordando; 14:45 Lima 2471 Cancelado; 15:10 Monterrey 318 A tiempo.

choices: El vuelo a Monterrey habrá salido tarde.
El vuelo a Cancún estará cancelado.
Los pasajeros de Bogotá ya habrán aterrizado.
Los pasajeros del vuelo a Lima estarán molestos.
questions.explanation: The Lima flight is "Cancelado", so it's a fair guess that its passengers are probably upset: "estarán molestos" (future of probability). The Monterrey flight is on time ("A tiempo"), the Cancún flight is boarding ("Abordando"), and the Bogotá flight is delayed until 15:30, so it hasn't even left.

questions.stem: Complete with the future perfect of "pasar": "¿Sin zapatos? ¿Qué le ___?"
questions.explanation: Wondering about something that has just happened takes the future perfect: "¿Qué le habrá pasado?" (I wonder what's happened to him). It's "haber" in the future, "habrá", + the participle "pasado".

questions.stem: Complete with "estar": "Lo más probable es que ___ esperando el equipaje."
questions.explanation: "Lo más probable es que" takes the subjunctive, like "es probable que": "Lo más probable es que esté esperando el equipaje" (Most likely he's waiting for his luggage).

questions.stem: Wonder aloud with the future of probability of "ser": "¿Qué hora ___ en Madrid?"
questions.explanation: The simple future makes a guess about the present: "¿Qué hora será en Madrid?" (I wonder what time it is in Madrid). "¿Qué hora es?" would simply ask.

questions.stem: Match each expression with the mood that follows it.
questions.explanation: "Lo más probable es que" and "puede que" take the subjunctive; "a lo mejor" and "supongo que" the indicative; "quizás" either mood; "capaz que" (colloquial in much of Latin America) usually the indicative, though the DPD notes the subjunctive also occurs.

questions.stem: Which sentences are guesses about the past? Select all that apply.
choices: Estará en la fila de migración.
Tendría unos veinte años cuando se fue.
questions.explanation: "Serían" and "tendría" are the conditional of probability (guesses about the past); "habrá perdido" is the future perfect (a guess about the recent past). "Estará en la fila" is a guess about now, and "Mañana estará en Puebla" is a plain future.

questions.stem: Put the sentences in order from the most sure to the least sure.
questions.explanation: The present indicative states a fact; "debe de" + infinitive is a confident guess; "puede que" + subjunctive only allows a possibility; "¡Quién sabe!" admits you have no idea.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: He must have missed the connection in Bogotá.
questions.explanation: "Must have" + something recent is the future perfect: "habrá perdido". "Habría perdido" means "would have missed". The place can come last or first: "En Bogotá habrá perdido la conexión".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Most likely they'll arrive before it gets dark.
questions.explanation: "Lo más probable es que" takes the subjunctive, "lleguen", and "antes de que" always takes the subjunctive too (B1), "oscurezca" (from "oscurecer", like "conozca"). "Llegan" (indicative) is wrong after "lo más probable es que". The "antes de que" clause can also come before "lleguen" or open the sentence.

questions.stem: A Spanish speaker says "Eso es un tópico." What does "tópico" mean here?
questions.explanation: "El tópico" is a false friend: it means a commonplace or cliché ("Es un tópico decir que…"). "Topic" in Spanish is "el tema". ("Tópico" is also a medical word for something applied to the skin, but not in this sentence.)

questions.stem: Which sentence is the best hedged version of "Los mexicanos siempre llegan tarde"?
choices: Los mexicanos nunca llegan a tiempo.
En muchos casos, a las fiestas se llega más tarde de la hora de la invitación.
Todos los mexicanos llegan un poco tarde.
Es evidente que los mexicanos llegan tarde.
questions.explanation: The hedged version limits the claim ("en muchos casos"), the situation ("a las fiestas") and avoids naming a whole nation. "Nunca", "todos" and "es evidente que" all keep the all-or-nothing claim.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Hay quien piensa que en México se duerme la siesta.
Hay quien piense que en México se duerme la siesta.
Hay quien piensen que en México se duerme la siesta.
Hay quienes piensan que en México se duerme la siesta.
questions.explanation: "Hay quien" takes either mood: the indicative ("piensa") presents the people as real; the subjunctive ("piense") keeps them vaguer. "Quien" is singular, so the verb is singular; the plural is "hay quienes piensan".

questions.stem: "La mayoría de los mexicanos vive / viven en ciudades." Which verb is correct?
questions.explanation: After "la mayoría de" + a plural noun the verb can agree with "la mayoría" (singular "vive") or with the people (plural "viven"). Both are accepted. "Vivimos" isn't required, though a Mexican speaker who includes himself or herself may also say "La mayoría de los mexicanos vivimos en ciudades".

questions.stem: In the forum thread, how does Rulo_mty explain why many people avoid a direct "no"?
choices: It's not lying: in general, not hurting the other person is valued.
Saying "no" is rude in every situation.
questions.explanation: He says "No es que la gente mienta, sino que, por lo general, se valora no herir al otro", and advises asking again kindly. He hedges with "mucha gente", "a veces" and "por lo general".

questions.stem: According to Rulo_mty, how does punctuality work?
choices: Everyone is always on time in Querétaro.
It depends on the situation: later for a house party, on time for work or the doctor.
Only people from Monterrey are punctual.
questions.explanation: "Depende muchísimo de la situación": at a house party the normal thing is to arrive a while after the time, but for a work appointment or the doctor you're expected on time. He also notes some people are late for everything, "como en cualquier país".

questions.stem: INEGI reports that in 2020, 21% of Mexico's population lived in localities of fewer than 2,500 inhabitants. Which conclusion is stated carefully?
choices: Exactly 79% of Mexicans live in big cities.
Most Mexicans live in small villages.
About four in five people lived in larger localities.
questions.explanation: 100% − 21% = 79%, so "about four in five" lived in localities of 2,500 or more. That doesn't mean "big cities" (a town of 3,000 counts), and the figure is for 2020, not "today". Rural Mexico exists: about one in five lived there.

questions.stem: Complete: "Los jóvenes ___ a mudarse a las ciudades."
questions.explanation: "Tender a" + infinitive (to tend to) is a stem changer like "entender": "tiendo, tiende, tienden". "Tenden" misses the change, "tiendan" is subjunctive, and "tienen" comes from "tener".

questions.stem: Complete with "mentir": "No es que la gente ___, sino que se valora no herir al otro."
questions.explanation: "No es que" takes the subjunctive. "Mentir" is an e → ie stem changer: "miento" → "mienta". The real reason after "sino que" is in the indicative: "se valora".

questions.stem: Complete with "ser": "A las fiestas se llega tarde, pero eso no significa que la gente ___ impuntual en el trabajo."
questions.explanation: "No significa que" denies a conclusion, so, like "no creo que", it takes the subjunctive: "no significa que la gente sea impuntual".

questions.stem: Match each word with its meaning.
questions.explanation: "El prejuicio" is a judgment made in advance; "etiquetar" is to label (also to tag in a photo); "la idiosincrasia" is the shared character of a group; "generalizar" is to generalize (preterite "generalicé"); "la diversidad" is diversity. "Topic" would be "el tema", not "el tópico".

questions.stem: Put the sentences of this answer to a stereotype in the order the lesson recommends: concede, limit, give a fact, conclude.
choices: Es cierto que hay muchos pueblos pequeños.
Pero no es que todo el país sea rural.
Según el INEGI, en 2020 el 21 % de la población vivía en localidades de menos de 2500 habitantes.
Es decir, alrededor de cuatro de cada cinco personas vivían en localidades más grandes.
questions.explanation: First concede what is true ("Es cierto que…"), then limit it ("no es que" + subjunctive), then give a sourced, dated fact, and finally draw a careful conclusion with "es decir" and "alrededor de".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Not all people from Mexico City drive badly.
questions.explanation: "No todos" limits the claim; the verb is an ordinary indicative statement: "No todos los chilangos manejan mal" (also, more colloquially, "Los chilangos no todos manejan mal"). ("Chilango" is informal for someone from Mexico City.) "Manejen" (subjunctive) has no trigger here.

questions.stem: Which sentence presents a stereotype as a claim, not as a fact?
choices: Se dice que los regios son tacaños.
Es verdad que los regios son tacaños.
questions.explanation: "Se dice que…" reports what people say without making it your own claim. The other three assert it in your own voice, and two of them make it stronger ("es verdad", "todos").

questions.stem: In the diary, why did Joaquín feel sick on Monday?
choices: He had left his hat in the truck and got the start of sunstroke.
He drank water from the river.
He got bitten by an insect.
questions.explanation: "Había dejado el sombrero en la camioneta": the pluperfect explains the cause before the moment of the story. Mariana thinks it was "el principio de una insolación" (the start of sunstroke).

questions.stem: Why did Paulina get dehydrated on Tuesday?
choices: They ran out of water completely.
She had sunstroke from the day before.
She had hardly drunk any water because she didn't feel thirsty.
The water from the stream made her sick.
questions.explanation: "No había tomado casi nada de agua porque, según ella, no tenía sed." Mariana adds: "Así es como uno se deshidrata sin darse cuenta" (that's how you get dehydrated without noticing).

questions.stem: What saved the group from the river on Wednesday?
choices: Chayo made them climb to a rock terrace away from the river.
They crossed the river before it rose.
questions.explanation: "Chayo nos hizo subir de inmediato a una terraza de piedra, lejos del río." On Thursday the rescue leader tells them: "Si no hubiéramos subido a la terraza…, nos habría alcanzado el río".

questions.stem: What does "Serían las cinco cuando vimos pasar troncos enteros" mean?
choices: It will be five when we see the tree trunks.
It would be five if we saw tree trunks.
It was exactly five when we saw the tree trunks.
It must have been about five when we saw whole tree trunks go by.
questions.explanation: The conditional of probability ("serían") is a guess about the past: "It must have been about five". The preterite "vimos" anchors it in the past. "Eran las cinco" would state the time as a fact.

questions.stem: In "Mi mamá ya habrá visto las noticias", what is Mariana doing?
choices: Describing what her mother will do tomorrow.
Guessing about something that has probably just happened.
Reporting what her mother told her.
Imagining a past that didn't happen.
questions.explanation: The future perfect ("habrá visto") guesses about the recent past: her mother must have seen the news by now. In the next sentence, "estará preocupadísima" guesses about the present.

questions.stem: Which is the impersonal report version of the diary's "Llamaron al 911"?
questions.explanation: An official report avoids the people involved and uses the impersonal or passive "se": "Se recibió una llamada al 911". The other versions keep a person, change the time, or turn the fact into a guess.

questions.stem: Why is the verb plural in "No se reportaron heridos"?
choices: Because the report is about four hikers.
Because "se" is always followed by a plural verb.
Because it is a guess about the past.
In the passive "se", the verb agrees with "heridos", the thing reported.
questions.explanation: With the passive "se" the verb agrees with the noun that is reported, here "heridos" (plural): "No se reportaron heridos". With one thing it's singular: "Se recibió una llamada". (With a person introduced by "a", the verb stays singular: "Se localizó al grupo".)

questions.stem: According to the lesson, what number do you call in an emergency in Mexico?
questions.explanation: The lesson gives 911 as Mexico's emergency number, in service since October 2016 and rolled out state by state. For trips, it also points to the Coordinación Nacional de Protección Civil, your state's civil protection office and the weather forecast.

questions.stem: Report the instruction "No se muevan" in the past: "Nos pidieron que no nos ___."
questions.explanation: After a past request ("nos pidieron que"), the command becomes the imperfect subjunctive, made from the preterite "movieron": "que no nos moviéramos" (or "moviésemos"). "Mover" changes its stem only in the present.

questions.stem: Rewrite "Nos encontraron a las dos y media" for the report: "El grupo fue ___ a las 14:30 horas." (Use the participle of "localizar".)
questions.explanation: The "ser" passive is "fue" + participle, and the participle agrees with the subject, "el grupo" (masculine singular): "fue localizado". The report also uses the 24-hour clock.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in this campsite.

image.alt: A campsite between two canyon walls at night: lightning in the sky; on the ground a sleeping bag, a campfire, a first-aid kit, a canteen and a compass. Six numbers mark the lightning, the sleeping bag, the fire, the first-aid kit, the canteen and the compass.

questions.explanation: The flash in the sky is "el relámpago"; on the ground are "la bolsa de dormir" (Spain "el saco de dormir"), "la fogata", "el botiquín" with its red cross, "la cantimplora" and "la brújula" (both from lesson 08). There is no harness or flashlight.

questions.stem: Match each form from the diary with what it does.
choices: a guess about the recent past
questions.explanation: The conditional ("serían") guesses about the past; the future perfect ("habrá visto") about the recent past; the future ("estará") about now; the pluperfect ("había dejado") tells what happened before the moment of the story.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: It must have been about two when Joaquín started to complain.
questions.explanation: A guess about a past time takes the conditional: "serían las dos" ("serán" would be a guess about now and clashes with "empezó"). The "cuando" clause can come first or last, and "Joaquín" can come before "empezó", between "empezó" and "a quejarse", or at the end.

questions.stem: Choose the relative: "El laboratorio ___ trabajó Leeuwenhoek era pequeño."
questions.explanation: The verb is "trabajar en": the preposition must come before the relative, so "en el que" (or "en el cual", or "donde"). Plain "que" drops the preposition, "quien" refers only to people, and "cuyo" means "whose".

questions.stem: Choose the right form: "Es una inventora ___ patentes se venden en todo el mundo."
questions.explanation: "Cuyo" agrees with the thing possessed, not with the owner. The thing possessed is "patentes" (feminine plural), so "cuyas", even though "inventora" is feminine singular.

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT correct Spanish?
choices: La mujer que inventó el aparato vive en Lyon.
La mujer quien inventó el aparato vive en Lyon.
La mujer, quien inventó el aparato, vive en Lyon.
La mujer con quien trabajé vive en Lyon.
questions.explanation: "Quien" can't start a restrictive clause (no commas) without a preposition: say "la mujer que inventó". With commas (a non-restrictive clause) or after a preposition ("con quien"), "quien" is correct.

questions.stem: Choose the relative: "No entiendo ___ dice el manual."
questions.explanation: Here the relative means "what": a free relative with no antecedent. Only "lo que" does that job. "Lo cual" needs an antecedent idea and a comma before it ("Llegó tarde, lo cual me molestó").

questions.stem: What does this sentence say? "Los inventores, que patentaron sus ideas, se hicieron ricos."
choices: Only the inventors who patented their ideas got rich.
The inventors got rich before they patented their ideas.
Some inventors got rich without patenting their ideas.
All the inventors patented their ideas, and they got rich.
questions.explanation: The commas make the clause non-restrictive: it adds a fact about all the inventors already mentioned. Without commas ("Los inventores que patentaron sus ideas se hicieron ricos"), it would pick out only those who patented.

questions.stem: Choose the right words: "La razón ___ renunció nunca se supo."
questions.explanation: After "la razón" Spanish uses "por" + a relative: "por la cual" (or "por la que"). "Porque" is a conjunction, not a relative; "cuya" needs a noun after it; "quien" refers to people.

questions.stem: Complete with the right form of cuyo: "Admiro a los científicos ___ descubrimientos salvan vidas."
questions.explanation: "Cuyo" agrees with "descubrimientos" (masculine plural), the thing possessed: "cuyos descubrimientos".

questions.stem: Choose the relative: "Esta es la colega con ___ escribí la patente."
questions.explanation: After a preposition, a person can be "quien" (or "la que", "la cual"). "Lo que" refers to an idea, not a person; "cuya" means "whose" and needs a noun; "cual" needs its article ("la cual").

questions.stem: Match each relative to what it is used for.
choices: whose: agrees with the thing possessed
a whole idea, after a comma
questions.explanation: "Cuyo" means whose; "lo cual" refers back to a whole idea ("Llegó tarde, lo cual me molestó"); "quien" is for people; "adonde" is for a destination ("el país adonde emigró"). A time is "cuando".

questions.stem: Name the inventions on the timeline.

image.alt: The inventions timeline from the lesson with the names of the inventions hidden. 1 is in the box hacia 1450, Gutenberg, Maguncia. 2 is in the box hacia 1590, ¿los Janssen? (se discute). 3 is in the box 1876, patente de Bell. 4 is in the box 1880, patente de Edison. 5 is in the box 1942, Lamarr y Antheil.

questions.explanation: Gutenberg's movable-type press (about 1450); the compound microscope, usually credited to the Janssens (disputed); Bell's telephone patent (1876); Edison's light bulb patent (1880); Lamarr and Antheil's frequency-hopping patent (1942).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Gutenberg, whose press changed Europe, worked in Mainz.
questions.explanation: "Gutenberg, cuya imprenta cambió Europa, trabajó en Maguncia." The non-restrictive clause sits between commas right after "Gutenberg", and "cuya" agrees with "imprenta" (feminine), not with Gutenberg.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: That's the reason why she resigned.
questions.explanation: "Esa es la razón por la cual renunció." After "la razón", use "por" + a relative ("por la cual" or "por la que"); "porque" is a conjunction and can't follow "la razón" here.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Es el mejor invento que se ha hecho.
Es el mejor invento que se haya hecho.
Es el mejor invento el cual se ha hecho.
Es el mejor invento quien se ha hecho.
