questions.explanation: After a superlative both moods are correct; the subjunctive ("se haya hecho") sounds more emphatic. "El cual" can't start a restrictive clause without a preposition, and "quien" is only for people.

questions.stem: Choose the connector: "Nos mudamos a Toluca ___ subió la renta."
questions.explanation: After the main clause, the cause goes with "porque". Causal "como" only works at the start ("Como subió la renta, nos mudamos"). "De ahí que" and "por ende" introduce a consequence, not a cause.

questions.stem: Choose the form the lesson teaches for a rejected cause: "Se fue no porque ___, sino porque no podía pagar."
questions.explanation: A cause the speaker rejects ("no porque…") goes in the subjunctive; after a past main verb ("se fue"), the imperfect subjunctive: "quisiera". The real cause, after "sino porque", is in the indicative ("no podía"). The indicative "quería" is also heard, but it can be misread as the real cause; "quiera" breaks the sequence of tenses, and "querría" is a conditional.

questions.stem: Complete with the form the lesson recommends: "Los precios suben; de ahí que mucha gente ___ a la periferia."
questions.explanation: "De ahí que" is normally followed by the subjunctive, because the result is presented as already known: "se mude". You may occasionally read it with the indicative (the DPD notes both), but the subjunctive is the form to produce.

questions.stem: Choose the word: "Hay ___ departamentos vacíos que la calle parece abandonada."
questions.explanation: Before a noun, use "tanto" agreeing with it: "departamentos" is masculine plural, so "tantos". "Tan" goes before adjectives and adverbs ("tan caro").

questions.stem: Which connector of consequence is the most formal?
questions.explanation: "Por ende" (therefore, hence) belongs to formal, mostly written Spanish. "Así que", "por eso" and "entonces" are everyday choices.

questions.stem: Choose the words: "___ tráfico, llegué tarde a la entrevista."
questions.explanation: The traffic caused a bad result, so "por culpa del tráfico". "A pesar del" means "despite", which doesn't fit; "debido a que" and "como" need a verb after them ("debido a que había tráfico").

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "La colonia ha cambiado ___ que ya no la reconozco."
questions.explanation: After a verb, the intensity is "tanto que": "ha cambiado tanto que ya no la reconozco". "Tan" would need an adjective or adverb after it.

questions.stem: Match each connector to what it does.
choices: gives a cause, before the main clause
gives a cause with a good result
gives a consequence in formal writing
questions.explanation: Causal "como" comes first; "de ahí que" draws a consequence and usually takes the subjunctive; "gracias a que" credits a cause with a good result; "por ende" is a formal "therefore". Purpose is "para que", "a fin de que".

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Como no había metro, tomamos un taxi.
Tomamos un taxi como no había metro.
Tomamos un taxi porque no había metro.
Tomamos un taxi, ya que no había metro.
questions.explanation: Causal "como" must come before the main clause, so the second sentence is wrong. "Porque" follows the main clause, and "ya que" can go before or after it.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Since the rent went up, we moved.
questions.explanation: "Como subió la renta, nos mudamos" (or "Como la renta subió…"): causal "como" opens the sentence and takes the indicative. The main clause states a fact, so "nos mudamos", not the subjunctive.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Downtown is very expensive, which is why so many students live far away.
questions.explanation: "El centro es carísimo; de ahí que tantos estudiantes vivan lejos." "De ahí que" usually takes the subjunctive ("vivan"); the subject can also follow the verb ("de ahí que vivan lejos tantos estudiantes"). "Estudiantes" is masculine here, so "tantos".

questions.stem: In the news feature, why did doña Ofelia leave Jardines del Río?
choices: She wanted a quieter place to live.
Her fonda closed for lack of customers.
questions.explanation: She says "No me fui porque quisiera, sino porque me pidieron el doble": she didn't leave because she wanted to, but because they asked her for twice the rent.

questions.stem: Choose the verb: "Una vez que te ___ de alta, descansa una semana."
questions.explanation: "Una vez que" pointing to the future takes the subjunctive: "te den de alta". The indicative is for the past or habits ("Una vez que me dieron de alta, me fui a casa"); the future is never used after it.

questions.stem: Choose the verb: "Me pusieron la anestesia antes de que ___ el cirujano."
questions.explanation: "Antes de que" always takes the subjunctive, even in the past; after a past main verb, the imperfect subjunctive: "entrara".

questions.stem: Choose the connector: "___ empecé la rehabilitación, camino mejor."
questions.explanation: "Desde que" (since) marks a real starting point and takes the indicative: "Desde que empecé…". The other three take the subjunctive and don't fit the meaning.

questions.stem: Choose the words: "Se suspendieron las visitas ___ prevenir contagios."
questions.explanation: Before an infinitive ("prevenir"), use "con el fin de" (or "a fin de", "para"). "A fin de que" and "para que" need a conjugated verb in the subjunctive, and "no vaya a ser que" expresses a precaution with a subjunctive.

questions.stem: Choose the verb: "Lleva la receta, no vaya a ser que te la ___."
questions.explanation: "No vaya a ser que" (in case) always takes the subjunctive: "te la pidan".

questions.stem: What does this mean? "A medida que baje la inflamación, podrás doblar la rodilla."
choices: Before the swelling goes down, you can bend your knee.
Unless the swelling goes down, you won't bend your knee.
As the swelling goes down, you'll be able to bend your knee.
Since the swelling has gone down, you can bend your knee.
questions.explanation: "A medida que" means "as" for two things that change together; with the subjunctive ("baje") it points to the future.

questions.stem: Complete with the present subjunctive of sentir (tú): "Cada vez que ___ dolor, tómate el analgésico."
questions.explanation: "Sentir" changes e to ie in the subjunctive: "sientas". "Cada vez que" about the future takes the subjunctive.

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "Llévate un suéter, no ___ que haga frío."
questions.explanation: "No sea que" is the short form of "no vaya a ser que": a precaution, "in case it gets cold". It takes the subjunctive ("haga").

questions.stem: Put the steps of Héctor's treatment in order, from the timeline and the discharge sheet.
choices: Tiene consulta con el especialista antes de volver a correr.
questions.explanation: Surgery on day 0, discharge on day 2, the stitches come out on day 10 (13 de marzo), physical therapy from week 2 to week 8, and a visit to the specialist before he runs again.

questions.stem: Name the hidden rows of the discharge sheet.

image.alt: The discharge sheet from the lesson with five row names hidden and numbered. 1: 5 de marzo de 2026. 2: Lesión de menisco, rodilla derecha. 3: Paracetamol 500 mg, una tableta cada 8 horas si hay dolor, máximo 5 días. 4: Reposo; no mojar la herida; iniciar rehabilitación una vez que se retiren los puntos. 5: 13 de marzo de 2026: retiro de puntos. The rows Paciente, Fecha de ingreso and Procedimiento are visible.

questions.explanation: The discharge date comes after the admission date; the diagnosis names the injury; the treatment gives the medicine and dose; the indicaciones are the instructions; the next appointment is the date to come back.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Once they discharge you, rest for a week.
questions.explanation: "Una vez que te den de alta, descansa una semana" (or with the time clause second). It points to the future, so the subjunctive "te den", not "te dan".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Take the prescription in case they ask to see it.
questions.explanation: "Lleva la receta, no vaya a ser que te pidan verla." The precaution usually follows the main clause and always takes the subjunctive ("te pidan").

questions.stem: Choose the verb: "El juicio será en marzo, a no ser que ___ a un acuerdo."
questions.explanation: "A no ser que" (unless), like "a menos que", always takes the subjunctive: "lleguen".

questions.stem: Choose the verb: "Guarda todos los recibos, por si ___ un problema."
questions.explanation: "Por si" is built on "si", so it never takes the present subjunctive or the future: "por si hay" (or, for a less likely case, "por si hubiera").

questions.stem: What does this mean? "Como no pagues la renta, te demandan."
choices: If you don't pay the rent, they'll sue you (a warning).
Since you didn't pay the rent, they sued you.
Even if you pay the rent, they'll sue you.
Whenever you don't pay the rent, they sue you.
questions.explanation: "Como" + subjunctive at the start is a condition that sounds like a warning or threat. With the indicative, "como" gives a cause: "Como no pagaste la renta, te demandaron" (since you didn't pay).

questions.stem: Choose the verb: "El contrato era bueno, excepto que no ___ nada del depósito."
questions.explanation: Here "excepto que" means "except that" and introduces a fact, so it takes the indicative: "no decía nada". With the subjunctive, "excepto que" means "unless".

questions.stem: Which connector belongs above all to contracts and laws?
questions.explanation: "En el supuesto de que" (in the event that) is the formal choice of contracts and laws; in conversation people say "en caso de que" or "si".

questions.stem: What does this mean? "De seguir así, perderán el juicio."
choices: Because they carry on like this, they lost the case.
If they carry on like this, they'll lose the case.
After carrying on like this, they lost the case.
Although they carry on like this, they won't lose the case.
questions.explanation: "De" + infinitive is a compact "if": "De seguir así" = "Si siguen así". The future "perderán" gives the result.

questions.stem: Complete with the present subjunctive of incumplir (ellos): "En caso de que ___ el contrato, los demandamos."
questions.explanation: "En caso de que" takes the subjunctive: "incumplan" (from incumplir, a regular -ir verb).

questions.stem: Match each connector to its meaning.
questions.explanation: "A condición de que" sets a requirement; "salvo que" an exception; "en el supuesto de que" a possible case (formal); "por si acaso" a precaution. "Although" would be "aunque".

questions.stem: Name the people in the courtroom.

image.alt: The courtroom from the lesson without labels. 1 is on the raised bench at the back, where a person sits in front of a Mexican flag. 2 is on the witness stand at the left. 3 is on the table at the front left, where one person sits. 4 and 5 are on the table at the front right, where two people sit side by side: 4 under the person in a blue jacket and 5 under the person in a light jacket.

questions.explanation: The judge sits on the raised bench; the witness on the stand; the prosecutor at the left table; the defense lawyer and the defendant side by side at the right table, as in the lesson's picture.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Te lo rento siempre y cuando lo cuides.
Te lo rento siempre y cuando lo cuidas.
questions.explanation: "Siempre y cuando" always takes the subjunctive ("lo cuides"). "Por si" follows "si": indicative ("por si llueve") or imperfect subjunctive ("por si lloviera"), never the present subjunctive.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'll accept the agreement on condition that it's put in writing.
questions.explanation: "Acepto el acuerdo a condición de que quede por escrito" (the condition can also come first). "A condición de que" takes the subjunctive: "quede".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: If they carry on like this, they'll lose the case.
questions.explanation: "De seguir así, perderán el juicio": "de" + infinitive works as "if". It usually comes first, but "Perderán el juicio de seguir así" is also correct. After "de" the verb stays in the infinitive.

questions.stem: In a Mexican regulation, what does "artículo 8, fracción III" point to?
choices: The third numbered subsection of article 8
The third chapter of the law
questions.explanation: A fracción is a numbered part of an article, written in Roman numerals: fracción III is the third one in article 8.

questions.stem: In "El condómino pagará la cuota dentro de los primeros diez días", the future "pagará" expresses…
questions.explanation: In laws and regulations the future states a duty, like English "shall": the owner shall pay the fee.

questions.stem: An old law says "el que infringiere esta disposición". What is the modern equivalent?
questions.explanation: "Infringiere" is a future subjunctive; modern Spanish uses the present subjunctive in its place: "el que infrinja" (whoever breaks).

questions.stem: In "La falta de pago de dos o más cuotas consecutivas dará lugar a un recargo", what is the subject of "dará"?
choices: la falta de pago (de dos o más cuotas consecutivas)
questions.explanation: Everything before the verb is the subject, and its core is "la falta de pago" (failure to pay); the rest describes it. That's why the verb is singular ("dará"), not plural.

questions.stem: According to article 9 of the condominium regulation, which is NOT a condition for keeping a pet?
choices: It must be registered with the administration.
It must be on a leash in the common areas.
Its owner must pick up its waste.
It must be vaccinated every year.
questions.explanation: Article 9 lists three conditions after "siempre y cuando": registration, a leash in common areas, and picking up waste. It says nothing about vaccines.

questions.stem: In the worked example, why does Mariana get no fine for her dog walking without a leash?
choices: Pets are allowed everywhere without restriction.
Article 11 fines only breaches of article 8.
Tenants don't have to follow the regulation.
questions.explanation: The leash rule is in article 9, but article 11 sets fines only for the bans in article 8. Tenants are bound (article 10), and "first offense" matters only for doubling a fine.

questions.stem: Under Mexico's federal consumer law (article 77), a warranty offered with a product or service can't be shorter than…
questions.explanation: The lesson's summary of the LFPC: "La garantía no podrá ser inferior a noventa días" (counted from delivery). Check the current text before citing it, since laws change.

questions.stem: What does "Se deroga el reglamento anterior" mean?
questions.explanation: "Derogar" means to repeal: the old rules stop being in force. Laws announce it in their transitional articles.

questions.stem: Which sentence states a permission, not an obligation or a ban?
choices: Queda prohibido estacionar en las entradas.
El arrendatario deberá dar aviso por escrito.
questions.explanation: "Podrá" gives a right or permission. "Queda prohibido" bans; "deberá" and the future "pagará" impose duties.

questions.stem: Write the modern word for the future subjunctive "fuere": "cualquiera que fuere su causa" = "cualquiera que ___ su causa".
questions.explanation: The future subjunctive "fuere" is read as the present subjunctive "sea": "cualquiera que sea su causa" (whatever its cause may be).

questions.stem: Match each part of a Mexican law to its description.
choices: a large division that groups several articles
a numbered part of an article, in Roman numerals
a part of a fracción, marked with a letter
says when the law comes into force
questions.explanation: Laws go from títulos and capítulos down to artículos, fracciones (I, II, III) and incisos (a, b, c); the transitorios at the end set the date of entry into force and what is repealed. A court ruling is "una sentencia".

questions.stem: Put the parts in order from the largest to the smallest.
questions.explanation: A law contains chapters, chapters contain articles, an article can have fracciones, and a fracción can have incisos.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The new regulations come into force on January 1.
questions.explanation: "El nuevo reglamento entra en vigor el primero de enero." The subject can also follow the verb, and the date can open the sentence ("El primero de enero entra en vigor el nuevo reglamento"). The indicative states a fact; "entre" is a subjunctive.

questions.stem: Who received half of the 1947 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine?
questions.explanation: Bernardo Houssay, an Argentine physiologist, for discovering the role of a hormone of the anterior pituitary lobe in sugar metabolism. Leloir won the Chemistry prize in 1970 and Molina in 1995; Miramontes never received a Nobel.

questions.stem: Which statement about Rodolfo Neri Vela reports the source accurately?
choices: He was the first Latin American in space.
He was an astronomer at the UNAM.
He was the first Mexican to take part in a NASA space mission.
He built the Morelos II satellite.
questions.explanation: The UNAM source calls him the first Mexican to take part in a NASA space mission. He was an engineer, not an astronomer; Morelos II was one of three satellites put into orbit on his mission, and "first Latin American in space" is a different, broader claim.

questions.stem: Choose the right form: "Mario Molina, ___ estudios sobre el ozono le valieron el premio Nobel, nació en la Ciudad de México."
questions.explanation: "Cuyo" agrees with "estudios", the thing possessed (masculine plural): "cuyos".

questions.stem: Choose the participle: "En 1940 le fue ___ una patente por un sistema de televisión a color."
questions.explanation: In a "ser" passive the participle agrees with the subject, "una patente" (feminine singular): "fue otorgada".

questions.stem: Which sentence reports the claim about González Camarena most carefully?
choices: González Camarena inventó la televisión a color.
Nadie hizo televisión en color antes que González Camarena.
En México suele presentarse a González Camarena como el creador de la televisión a color.
La televisión a color fue inventada solo en México.
questions.explanation: It says who makes the claim and where, without turning it into the writer's own fact. Other inventors had shown color television before him, so the bare claims overstate.

questions.stem: What is true of Luis F. Leloir?
choices: He won the 1970 Nobel Prize in Chemistry alone.
He shared the 1995 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
He was born in Buenos Aires.
questions.explanation: Leloir, born in Paris in 1906, received the whole 1970 Chemistry prize for discovering sugar nucleotides. The 1995 prize was Molina's (shared); norethisterone was Miramontes's synthesis.

questions.stem: A biography says "Se le considera el primer latinoamericano galardonado con un Nobel en una ciencia." What does "se le considera" do?
choices: It reports a common view without the writer claiming it as proven.
It proves the fact with a document.
It asks whether the fact is true.
questions.explanation: "Se le considera" (he is considered) attributes the judgment to people in general. It's a careful way to report a claim, like "se le atribuye" or "según…".

questions.stem: What did Luis E. Miramontes achieve on October 15, 1951?
choices: He patented a color television system.
He synthesized norethisterone in the Syntex laboratories.
He received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
He put a satellite into orbit.
questions.explanation: While still a chemistry student, he synthesized norethisterone, a compound later used in some of the first birth control pills. The patent was registered in his name and those of Rosenkranz and Djerassi.

questions.stem: Complete with the right form of cuyo: "Houssay, ___ campo era la fisiología, nació en Buenos Aires."
questions.explanation: "Cuyo" agrees with "campo" (masculine singular), the thing possessed.

questions.stem: Match each person to what the sources say.
choices: half of the Nobel in Physiology or Medicine, 1947
questions.explanation: Houssay (1947) and Leloir (1970) were Argentine; Molina (1995) and Neri Vela (1985) Mexican. None of them won a Nobel in Physics.

questions.stem: Put the events in chronological order.
choices: González Camarena patents a color TV system in Mexico.
Neri Vela flies on the shuttle Atlantis.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The patent was registered in the name of three chemists.
questions.explanation: "La patente fue registrada a nombre de tres químicos" (a verb-first passive, "Fue registrada la patente…", and a fronted "A nombre de tres químicos fue registrada la patente" are also correct). The participle agrees with "la patente": "registrada".

questions.stem: Last month Ana said to you: "Quiero que vengas temprano a la boda." The wedding was last week. Report it: "Ana me dijo que ___ temprano a la boda."
questions.explanation: After a past reporting verb the present "quiero" becomes "quería", and the present subjunctive becomes the imperfect subjunctive: "quería que fuera" ("fuese" is also correct). "Venir" often becomes "ir" when the place has changed. "Quiere que vaya" would only fit if the wedding were still ahead; "iba" and "vendría" are indicative or conditional, but "querer que" needs the subjunctive.

questions.stem: Report this after a past verb: "No creo que lo hayan visto." → "Dijo que no creía que lo ___."
questions.explanation: The perfect subjunctive "hayan visto" moves back to the pluperfect subjunctive "hubieran visto" (or "hubiesen visto") once the main verb is past ("creía"). "No creer que" still needs the subjunctive, so the indicative "habían visto" and the conditional "habrían visto" are wrong, and "hayan visto" breaks the sequence of tenses.

questions.stem: The director said: "El domingo ya habremos terminado." Report what she said about the workers, with the conditional perfect of terminar: "Dijo que el domingo ya ___."
questions.explanation: The future perfect "habremos terminado" becomes the conditional perfect after a past reporting verb: "Dijo que el domingo ya habrían terminado" (they would have finished). "Habrán terminado" keeps the future, which doesn't shift.

questions.stem: Choose the verb that reports an excuse: "El conductor ___ que no había visto la señal."
questions.explanation: "Alegar que" + indicative gives a reason or an excuse: "Alegó que no había visto la señal" (he claimed he hadn't seen the sign). "Suplicar" (to beg) takes "que" + subjunctive, "amenazar" takes "con" + infinitive, and "animar" takes "a" + infinitive.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Me recomendó que tomo el metro.
Le reprochó que no lo hubiera llamado.
questions.explanation: "Animar a" + infinitive, "amenazar con" + infinitive and "reprochar que" + subjunctive are all right ("postularse" is lesson 17's "to apply for a job"). "Recomendar que" needs the subjunctive: "Me recomendó que tomara el metro". "Amenazar" takes "con", never "de".

questions.stem: Match each reporting verb to the pattern it takes in this lesson.
questions.explanation: "Me animó a participar"; "Amenazó con renunciar"; "Le suplicó que no lo publicara"; "Recalcó que no habría cambios". None of these verbs takes "de" + infinitive.

questions.stem: What does "Advirtió que no saliéramos" mean?
choices: He warned that we hadn't gone out.
He warned that we wouldn't go out.
He said we might go out.
He warned us not to go out.
questions.explanation: "Advertir que" + subjunctive reports an instruction (warn someone to do or not to do something). With the indicative it reports a fact: "Advirtió que no saldríamos" = he warned that we wouldn't go out. "No habíamos salido" would be needed for "we hadn't gone out".

questions.stem: Complete so it means "He insisted that I go with him": "Insistió en que lo ___."
questions.explanation: "Insistir en que" + subjunctive reports pressure on someone to act, and after a past verb that is the imperfect subjunctive: "acompañara" (or "acompañase"). With the indicative it would report a claim about facts: "Insistió en que lo acompañaba" = he insisted that I was going with him.

questions.stem: In the lesson's news story, which verb does the reporter use for the director's "Este año no habrá ningún cambio en las tarifas. Se lo puedo asegurar"?
questions.explanation: The story says "recalcó que este año no habría cambios en las tarifas": "recalcar" (to stress) fits an assurance repeated with emphasis. "Negó" reports the denial about the week-long outage, "puntualizó" the added detail about the twenty water trucks, and nobody begs.

questions.stem: Label the numbered parts of the press conference.

image.alt: A press conference with four numbered parts: a woman speaking at a podium, the microphones in front of her, a stack of printed papers on a side table, and a TV camera on a tripod.

questions.explanation: The spokesperson (A2's el vocero, la vocera) speaks at the podium into the microphones; the press releases (el comunicado) lie on the table; the camera films. La primicia is a scoop and el entrevistado an interviewee: neither is shown.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: She begged him not to publish it.
questions.explanation: "Suplicar que" + subjunctive, imperfect after a past verb: "Le suplicó que no lo publicara" ("publicase" is also correct). "Le" (to him) is usual; "Suplicó que no lo publicara" is also accepted. The indicative "publicaba" would report a fact, not a plea.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The director stressed that there would be no changes.
questions.explanation: "Recalcar que" + indicative; the future "no habrá" becomes the conditional "no habría" after a past verb. The subject can also follow the verb, as often in news: "Recalcó la directora que no habría cambios". "Hubo" (there were) is a past fact, not "would be".

questions.stem: Your friend didn't hear you ask "¿Vienes mañana?" How do you repeat the question in conversation?
questions.explanation: Spoken Spanish repeats a question with "que" in front, and a yes / no question keeps "si": "¿Que si vienes mañana?" (I said, are you coming tomorrow?). This "que" has no accent: it isn't "what". The echo "que" belongs to speech, not to written reports.

questions.stem: Complete: "La reforma ___ por el Congreso la semana pasada."
questions.explanation: A finished event with an agent ("por el Congreso"): ser in the preterite + a participle agreeing with "la reforma": "fue aprobada". "Aprobado" doesn't agree, "sido" never changes, and "estar" + participle describes a state, which can't take "la semana pasada" and an agent like this.

questions.stem: Complete with the future passive: "El nuevo museo ___ en mayo."
questions.explanation: Ser in the future + the participle agreeing with "el museo" (masculine): "será inaugurado". "Inaugurada" is feminine, "habrá inaugurado" is an active future perfect with no subject to do it, and "es inaugurando" mixes ser with a gerund.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Se venden casas en esta colonia.
Se vende casas en esta colonia.
Se venden a casas en esta colonia.
questions.explanation: With the passive se the verb agrees with the thing: "Se venden casas". You will see "Se vende casas" on signs, but the DPD says the verb must agree with the plural. "A" is only used before people, so "a casas" and "a las casas" are wrong.

questions.stem: Complete with the impersonal se: "Ayer se ___ a los sospechosos."
questions.explanation: The impersonal se has no subject, so the verb stays singular even with "a" + plural people: "Se detuvo a los sospechosos". "Se detuvieron a los sospechosos" mixes the passive and the impersonal constructions, which the DPD rejects. The imperfect "detenían" doesn't fit "ayer" for one event, and "detuvieran" is subjunctive.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct standard Spanish? Select all that apply.
choices: Me robaron la cartera en el metro.
questions.explanation: "Se vive bien" is the impersonal se with a verb that has no object; "fueron publicados" agrees with "los resultados"; "Me robaron la cartera" is the third-person plural for an unknown thief. "Se detuvieron a…" should be "Se detuvo a tres personas", and "sido" never agrees: "ha sido aprobada".

questions.stem: Match each headline or sentence to the structure it uses.
left: La ley fue aprobada por el Senado
choices: a noun instead of a verb
questions.explanation: Headlines drop ser ("Detenido…"), use the present third-person plural for the authorities ("Aprueban…") or a noun ("Aprobación de…"). A full sentence with ser + participle + por is the ser passive. An impersonal se with a person would be "Se detuvo al presunto responsable".

questions.stem: What does "Dicen que va a llover" mean?
choices: People say it's going to rain.
I say it's going to rain.
It was said that it rained.
questions.explanation: The third-person plural with no subject is an unknown or general "they": "Dicen que…" = people say, they say. It never includes the speaker, it's in the present, and "va a llover" is a future.

questions.stem: In the lesson's news story, why does the reporter write that the two men "habrían vendido la pieza como chatarra"?
choices: It's a condition: "if they had sold it".
It's a polite way to report a request.
It refers to a sale that will happen in the future.
The claim isn't proven yet: it means "allegedly sold".
questions.explanation: News uses this conditional for something an authority claims but no court has confirmed, like "presunto" (alleged). The lesson asks you to recognize it; in your own writing "según la fiscalía" or "supuestamente" says the same thing more plainly.

questions.stem: What does the sensationalist version of the story add to the news story?
choices: Emotion and a judgment, but no new facts
A correction of the news story
questions.explanation: The sensationalist version has nothing the news story doesn't have; it adds emotion ("¡Qué sacrilegio!", "unos sinvergüenzas", "indignados") and a judgment (it calls the men "los ladrones" although no court has said so).

questions.stem: Label the numbered parts of the front page.

image.alt: The front page of El Diario del Valle with four numbered parts: the large headline, the photo of a bell, the line of small text under the photo, and the opinion column on the right.

questions.explanation: El titular (A2) is the headline; la foto carries el pie de foto (the caption) underneath; la columna (B1 honors) is the opinion piece on the right. La tirada is the print run and el comunicado a press release: neither is a part of the page.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish with the impersonal se.
questions.prompt: The suspects were arrested.
questions.explanation: Impersonal se with "a" + people and a singular verb: "Se detuvo a los sospechosos". "Se detuvieron a los sospechosos" mixes two constructions, and without "a" ("Se detuvieron los sospechosos") it would sound as if they stopped themselves.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The museum will be inaugurated in May.
questions.explanation: Ser in the future + a participle agreeing with "el museo": "El museo será inaugurado en mayo". Spanish word order is free here: "en mayo" can open or close the sentence, and the subject can follow the verb, as news often does ("Será inaugurado el museo en mayo"). "Inaugurada" is feminine.

questions.stem: Rewrite with the passive se: "Publicaron los resultados ayer." → "___ los resultados ayer."
questions.explanation: The passive se agrees with the thing: "Se publicaron los resultados ayer" (the results were published yesterday). "Se publicó los resultados" doesn't agree; the DPD recommends agreement.

questions.stem: Complete: "¡Ay! ___ los vasos." (I dropped the glasses.)
questions.explanation: Accidental se: se + me + a verb agreeing with the thing. "Los vasos" is plural, so "se me cayeron". "Se me cayó" would need one glass. "Se" always comes first, and the pronouns go before the conjugated verb.

questions.stem: Complete with the accidental se: "___ la sal." (We forgot the salt.)
questions.explanation: Se + nos (the people affected) + a verb agreeing with "la sal" (singular): "Se nos olvidó la sal". "Olvidamos la sal" is also correct Spanish, but it isn't the accidental se the question asks for.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: El mole le hace mi abuela.
El mole lo hace mi abuela.
Lo el mole hace mi abuela.
questions.explanation: A direct object placed before the verb is repeated with lo / la / los / las (clitic doubling): "El mole lo hace mi abuela" (my grandmother makes the mole). Without "lo" it reads as if the mole made the grandmother. "Le" is an indirect-object pronoun, and a pronoun can't go before an article.

questions.stem: Complete: "¿Le diste el libro a Ana? —Sí, ya ___ di."
questions.explanation: Le becomes se before lo, la, los, las: "se lo di" (I gave it to her). "Lo" stands for "el libro", so "la" is wrong, and the indirect pronoun always comes first.

questions.stem: What kind of se is in "Se comió todo el pastel"?
questions.explanation: With verbs of eating and drinking, se adds a sense of completeness ("he ate up the whole cake"); without it the facts are the same ("Comió todo el pastel"). It isn't passive (someone is the subject), reciprocal (no "each other") or accidental (no me / te / le, and eating a cake is deliberate).

questions.stem: Match each sentence to the kind of se it uses.
questions.explanation: "Se escriben" = they write to each other; "se me quemó" = accidental se with me; "se lo di" = le lo → se lo; "se venden tamales" agrees with the thing (passive se); "irse" means to leave, a different meaning from "ir". An impersonal se with a person would look like "Se detuvo a los sospechosos".

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Se la voy a pedir a Mari.
Voy a se la pedir a Mari.
questions.explanation: With a periphrasis the pronouns go before the conjugated verb or attach to the infinitive ("Se la voy a pedir / Voy a pedírsela"), never between. They attach to an affirmative command ("Pásamela") but go before a negative one: "No se lo des".

questions.stem: A Mexican friend says about her parents: "Ya se los dije." What does she most likely mean?
choices: I already said goodbye to them.
questions.explanation: Because se doesn't show the plural, many Latin Americans move it onto lo: "se los dije" for "se lo dije (a ellos)". The DPD calls it frequent in many American countries and recommends "se lo" in careful speech; recognize it, write "se lo".

questions.stem: You read in a novel from Madrid: "A Juan le vi ayer." What is this?
choices: A mistake in every variety of Spanish
Spain's leísmo: le as a direct object for a man, accepted by the RAE; Latin America says lo
questions.explanation: Leísmo uses le for a direct object, common in much of Spain; the RAE accepts it for a masculine singular person. The Latin American standard, and this course, use lo: "A Juan lo vi ayer".

questions.stem: In Mexico, what does "Se me hace que va a llover" mean?
choices: I think it's going to rain.
It's going to rain on me.
questions.explanation: "Se me hace que" is an everyday Mexican way to say "I think, it seems to me", like "me parece que", and it takes the indicative.

questions.stem: Label the numbered things in the kitchen.

image.alt: A Mexican kitchen with four numbered things: a flat round griddle with tortillas on the stove, a tall clay pot steaming on the stove, a three-legged stone mortar with a pestle on the counter, and a ladle hanging on the wall.

questions.explanation: The tortillas heat on el comal; la olla (A2) is the clay pot; el molcajete is the stone mortar for salsa; el cucharón (lesson 21) is the ladle. El metate is a sloping grinding stone for corn, and la báscula is a bathroom scale (lesson 16): neither is shown.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish with the accidental se.
questions.prompt: I burned the rice (by accident).
questions.explanation: Se + me + a verb agreeing with "el arroz": "Se me quemó el arroz", or with the subject first, "El arroz se me quemó". "Quemé el arroz" is correct Spanish too, but it doesn't use the accidental se, and "se me quemé" mixes the two.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'm going to explain it to you (tú).
questions.explanation: With a periphrasis the pronouns go before the conjugated verb ("Te lo voy a explicar") or attach to the infinitive ("Voy a explicártelo", with an accent to keep the stress on -car-). Both orders are correct.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ un año entrenando." (I've been training for a year.)
questions.explanation: "Llevar" + time + gerund says how long something has been going on: "Llevo un año entrenando". "Hace" needs "que" and a conjugated verb ("Hace un año que entreno"), and "estar" and "seguir" don't take a length of time this way.

questions.stem: Complete so it means "I still don't understand the routine": "Sigo ___ entender la rutina."
questions.explanation: "Seguir sin" + infinitive is the negative of "seguir" + gerund: "Sigo sin entender" = I still don't understand. "Sigo no entendiendo" is heard but much less natural.

questions.stem: Complete so it means "I started running again after the injury": "Volví ___ correr después de la lesión."
questions.explanation: "Volver a" + infinitive means to do something again. "Volví de correr" is also Spanish, but it means "I came back from running", which isn't the meaning asked for.

questions.stem: Complete with the periphrasis of gradual change: "Poco a poco ___ mejorando."
questions.explanation: "Ir" + gerund describes a change that builds up step by step: "Poco a poco voy mejorando". "Volver" and "dejar" take an infinitive with a preposition ("vuelvo a", "dejo de"), and "llevar" + gerund needs a length of time.

questions.stem: What does "Anda diciendo que va a correr un maratón" suggest?
choices: He said it once, a long time ago.
He's going around telling people he'll run a marathon, and the speaker sounds a bit critical.
He'll say it after the marathon.
questions.explanation: "Andar" + gerund means going around doing something, often with a critical or ironic tone. It has nothing to do with walking.

questions.stem: In Mexico, what does "El camión está por salir" mean?
choices: The bus is about to leave.
The bus still has to be cleaned.
The bus is leaving through the gate.
The bus is in favor of leaving.
questions.explanation: In Mexico and some other Latin American countries "estar por" + infinitive with an event means "to be about to", like "estar a punto de". It can also mean "still to be done" ("La cocina está por limpiar"), the sense used in Spain, but that needs a verb whose action is done to the subject, like "limpiar".

questions.stem: Which sentences put the pronoun in a correct place? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: With a periphrasis the pronoun goes before the conjugated verb or attaches to the gerund or infinitive: "Lo sigo intentando / Sigo intentándolo", "Lo dejé de hacer / Dejé de hacerlo". It never goes between the two verbs, and "de" can't move to the end.

questions.stem: Match each periphrasis to its meaning.
choices: to go so far as, to manage
questions.explanation: "Se puso a estirar" (started); "Dejé de comer azúcar" (stopped); "Volví a correr" (again); "Acabé cambiando de entrenador" (ended up); "Llegué a correr veinte kilómetros" (managed). "To be about to" is "estar a punto de" or, in much of Latin America, "estar por".

questions.stem: What does "Tengo pensado inscribirme en la carrera" mean?
choices: I thought about signing up yesterday.
I have to sign up for the race.
I've already signed up for the race.
I'm planning to sign up for the race.
questions.explanation: "Tener" + participle presents something already decided or done: "tengo pensado" = I've got it in mind, I'm planning. "Tengo que" would be an obligation. "La carrera" here is a race, a new sense of A2's degree course.

questions.stem: In Renata's diary, what happened in week 3?
choices: She got injured in a race.
She stalled and stopped running for a few days.
questions.explanation: Week 3 says "Me estanqué. Sigo sin pasar de cinco kilómetros… Dejé de correr unos días." She runs ten kilometers in week 6, and the diet is her next challenge; she never mentions an injury of her own.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I've been training for a year.
questions.explanation: "Llevar" + time + gerund: "Llevo un año entrenando"; the time can also come last: "Llevo entrenando un año". The infinitive "entrenar" is wrong after "llevar".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I keep trying (to do it).
questions.explanation: "Seguir" + gerund, with the pronoun before the conjugated verb ("Lo sigo intentando") or attached to the gerund ("Sigo intentándolo", with an accent). Both are correct.

questions.stem: In Renata's diary, "Mi entrenadora dice que la constancia vale más que la fuerza de voluntad." What does "la constancia" mean here?
questions.explanation: B1 taught "la constancia" as written proof (a certificate). Here, next to "la fuerza de voluntad" (willpower), it has its other sense: perseverance, keeping at something steadily.

questions.stem: The profile reports Itzel's "Todo empezó con una pregunta de mi sobrina" with a present verb. Complete: "Insiste en que todo ___ con una pregunta de su sobrina."
questions.explanation: After a present reporting verb nothing shifts, so the preterite she used stays: "insiste en que todo empezó". "Insistir en que" reports a claim, so it takes the indicative, not the subjunctive "empiece".

questions.stem: Complete the profile's sentence: "A las jóvenes les aconseja que no ___ a sentirse listas."
questions.explanation: "Aconsejar que" needs the subjunctive, and with a present main verb ("aconseja") the present subjunctive: "que no esperen". "Esperaran" would follow a past verb ("les aconsejó que no esperaran").

questions.stem: Why doesn't the profile put "Llevo quince años estudiando volcanes" in quotation marks?
choices: It was said off the record.
It's plain information, so it's better reported than quoted.
Spanish doesn't allow numbers inside quotations.
questions.explanation: Profiles keep quotation marks for what only that person could say in her own voice. A fact like fifteen years of work is reported: "Lleva quince años estudiando volcanes".

questions.stem: What did the newspaper do wrong when it quoted Itzel?
choices: It invented a quotation she never said.
It published something she said off the record.
It cut her sentence so that it said something different.
questions.explanation: She had said "no hay que tenerle miedo al volcán, sino respeto"; printing only the first half dropped the warning and changed the meaning. Cuts inside a quotation must not change what the person meant.

questions.stem: In "Ofelia fue mi primer referente", what does "referente" mean?
questions.explanation: "El referente" is a role model or benchmark: someone you measure yourself against. It is usually masculine even for a woman ("su primer referente"), though "una referente" is also heard.

questions.stem: Complete with the present subjunctive of animar: "Busca a alguien que te ___ cuando todo salga mal."
questions.explanation: A relative clause about someone not yet found takes the subjunctive: "alguien que te anime" (someone who will encourage you). "Animar" is regular: anime, animes, anime.

questions.stem: Which of these may a journalist do when quoting someone? Select all that apply.
choices: Leave out fillers like "este…" when they change nothing
Mark a cut inside a quotation with […]
Change a word inside the quotation marks so it sounds better
Print half of a sentence when the half says something else
Publish a correction when a quote turns out to be wrong
questions.explanation: Dropping fillers is common practice, a cut can be marked with […] as long as it doesn't change the meaning, and corrections should be public. Inside quotation marks the words must be the person's own, and a half sentence that changes the meaning is a distortion.

questions.stem: Match each reporting verb to what it suggests about the speaker.
choices: adds or corrects a precise detail
holds a view, often against others
questions.explanation: Each reporting verb is an interpretation of the original words. "Prometer" would be the verb for a promise; none of these four means that.

questions.stem: Why is "Les reprocha a algunos colegas que vean la divulgación como una pérdida de tiempo" a poor summary of Itzel's answer?
choices: It reports her words in the wrong tense.
It's too strong: she began by saying she understood them.
It quotes her without quotation marks.
questions.explanation: She said "Que los entiendo, pero que se equivocan". "Reprochar" (to reproach) turns a polite disagreement into blame. "Reprochar que" + subjunctive is grammatical; the problem is the tone. "Sostiene que contar la ciencia es tan necesario como hacerla" is fairer.

questions.stem: Where does the period go when a Spanish sentence ends with a quotation?
choices: After the closing quotation mark: …sino respeto".
Before the closing quotation mark: …sino respeto."
Both before and after the closing mark
Nowhere: the quotation mark replaces it
questions.explanation: Spanish puts the period after the closing quotation mark. US English puts it inside, which is a common mistake for English speakers writing Spanish.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: She insists that it all started with a question.
questions.explanation: "Insistir en que" + indicative reports a claim, and after a present verb nothing shifts: "Insiste en que todo empezó con una pregunta". The subject can also follow the verb: "…en que empezó todo con una pregunta". The subjunctive "empezara" would turn it into a demand.

questions.stem: In "¿Siempre supo que su vocación era la ciencia?", what does "la vocación" mean?
questions.explanation: "La vocación" is a vocation or calling: the work you feel drawn to. Vacation is "las vacaciones".

questions.stem: What kind of sentence is "Si no la hubiera conocido, seguramente estaría haciendo telenovelas"?
choices: A past condition with a past result
A real condition about the future
A mixed condition: a past condition with a present result
questions.explanation: The si clause is about the past (pluperfect subjunctive: if I hadn't met her) and the result is about now (conditional: I'd be making soap operas). That is lesson 04's mixed conditional.

questions.stem: Put these moments of Itzel's life in the order they happened.
choices: En la prepa quería ser actriz.
La maestra Ofelia la llevó a las faldas del volcán y la inspiró.
Su sobrina de seis años le preguntó si el volcán estaba enojado.
Grabó un video para explicárselo a su sobrina.
Ahora está terminando un libro dedicado a su sobrina.
questions.explanation: In high school she wanted to act until Ofelia's field trips inspired her; years later her six-year-old niece asked whether the volcano was angry, and Itzel recorded a video to explain it; now she's finishing a children's book dedicated to that niece. (Her thesis and the newspaper's mistake aren't dated against the video in the interview, so they aren't on the list.)

questions.stem: Where is "el bulo" the everyday word for a false story?
choices: In Spain; in Mexico you more often hear "noticia falsa" or "fake news"
questions.explanation: "Bulo" is the usual word in Spain (the DLE defines it as a false piece of news spread for some purpose). Mexican Spanish more often says "noticia falsa" (B1) or the English "fake news".

questions.stem: What is the yo preterite of verificar?
questions.explanation: C becomes qu before e to keep the k sound: "verifiqué". "Verificé" would sound like "verifisé", "verifiqé" lacks the u, and "verifique" without the accent is the subjunctive.

questions.stem: Complete with the preterite of viralizarse: "El video ___ en una noche."
questions.explanation: "Viralizarse" is a pronominal verb, so it keeps "se": "El video se viralizó" (went viral). Without "se" it would mean that the video made something else go viral.

questions.stem: In Example 2 (the flooded station), why is the post rated false?
choices: The photo was manipulated to add water.
The station really flooded that morning.
The post gave no date at all.
The photo is real, but it's from 2017 and another city.
questions.explanation: A reverse image search showed the photo was first published in 2017 during rains elsewhere, and the transit system confirmed the station was working normally. Nothing in the image was doctored: the lie was the date and the place.

questions.stem: The authorship of a message isn't confirmed yet. Which verb form does news writing use to report it with distance? "El mensaje ___ creado por una cuenta falsa."
questions.explanation: News uses the conditional ("habría sido creado": was allegedly created) for unconfirmed claims; recognize it. "Ha sido", "fue" and "es" state it as a fact. In your own writing, "según…" or "supuestamente" is a plainer way to keep the distance.

questions.stem: Which are warning signs that a post may be disinformation? Select all that apply.
choices: It tells you to share it at once before "they" delete it.
It names no source, or only "un amigo que trabaja en el gobierno".
It links to the full article on a named news site.
It is written in capital letters with many exclamation marks.
It gives the date and the author of the original report.
questions.explanation: Urgency, no source and shouting in capitals are the marks the lesson lists. A link to the original article, a date and an author are what a checkable post looks like, although they still need checking.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: "La captura de pantalla" is a screenshot, "manipular" to manipulate or doctor, "fiable" (also "confiable") reliable, "la desinformación" disinformation. A hoax is "el bulo".

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct in a fact-check?
questions.explanation: With "a" + people the impersonal se keeps the verb singular: "Se consultó a dos expertos". "Se consultaron a…" mixes the passive and the impersonal, and the "a" must come right before the people.

questions.stem: What does "una búsqueda inversa de imágenes" help you find?
choices: The text of the post in another language
The home address of whoever shared it
Where and when a picture appeared before
questions.explanation: A reverse image search looks for earlier copies of a picture, so you can see its original date and context.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The photo was taken in 2017.
questions.explanation: Ser passive with a participle agreeing with "la foto": "La foto fue tomada en 2017". The year can open the sentence and the subject can follow the verb ("Fue tomada la foto en 2017"). "Tomado" doesn't agree with "la foto".

questions.stem: Which word is used across Latin America with the same meaning as "fiable"?
questions.explanation: "Fiable" and "confiable" both mean reliable, trustworthy; "confiable" is very common in Latin America. "Confiado" means trusting (or overconfident), "la confianza" is trust, and "confidencial" is confidential.

questions.stem: What was Verificado 2018?
choices: A law against fake news passed in Mexico in 2018
A collaborative fact-checking project for Mexico's 2018 federal election
questions.explanation: Organized by Animal Político, AJ+ Español and Pop-Up Newsroom with about 90 partner organizations, it checked claims during the campaign for the July 1, 2018 election, including messages people sent by WhatsApp.

questions.stem: According to the lesson, why can a false story go viral before it is corrected?
choices: The algorithm shows people more of what they react to, and fear and anger get reactions.
Fact-checkers aren't allowed to publish for a week.
Corrections can only be published on paper.
questions.explanation: The lesson explains that a social network's algorithm favors what people react to, and messages built to provoke fear or anger travel fast; a check takes time.

questions.stem: Complete the correction: "En una versión anterior de esta nota ___ que el corte duraría una semana."
questions.explanation: The impersonal se with a "que" clause takes a singular verb: "se afirmaba que…" (it was stated that…). There's no plural subject for "afirmaban", no person to need "a", and "se" goes before a conjugated verb.

questions.stem: You correct yourself in mid-sentence: "Nos vemos el lunes, ___, el martes." Which marker fits?
questions.explanation: Mejor dicho (or rather) replaces what you just said with a more accurate word: Monday becomes Tuesday. Es más would add a stronger point, por cierto would open a side remark, and en fin wraps up a topic; none of them corrects a word.

questions.stem: "It looks like an easy job, but actually there's a lot of pressure." Complete: "Parece un trabajo fácil, pero ___ tiene mucha presión."
questions.explanation: En realidad sets the reality against an appearance (it looks easy, but in reality…). Actualmente is a false friend: it means "currently". Es más adds a stronger point for the same side, and total introduces the outcome of a story.

questions.stem: What does the speaker mean? "Me bajaron el sueldo y, encima, me cambiaron de horario."
choices: They cut my salary, but at least they changed my schedule.
They cut my salary because they changed my schedule.
They cut my salary, or rather, they changed my schedule.
They cut my salary and, on top of that, changed my schedule.
questions.explanation: Encima (colloquial) piles one complaint on another: on top of that. It doesn't soften the first problem, give a cause or correct it.

questions.stem: Best English for "En fin, así son las cosas."
choices: Oh well, that's how things are.
In fact, things are like that.
By the way, that's how things are.
questions.explanation: En fin wraps up a topic, often with a sigh of resignation: oh well, well, anyway. Here it isn't "finally" (the last item of a list usually takes por último or finalmente), "in fact" (de hecho) or "by the way" (por cierto).

questions.stem: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: La empresa de hecho, no despidió a nadie.
La empresa, de hecho no despidió a nadie.
La empresa, de hecho, no despidió a nadie.
La empresa de, hecho no despidió a nadie.
questions.explanation: A discourse marker in the middle of a sentence goes between two commas: La empresa, de hecho, no despidió a nadie. The other versions leave out one of the commas or split the marker itself.

questions.stem: You're writing a formal e-mail to a company about a problem. Which marker would sound out of place?
questions.explanation: Para colmo (to top it all off) is colloquial and sounds like a complaint over coffee. Asimismo and además add a point in any register, and es decir reformulates in any text.

questions.stem: What is "un puesto de planta" in Mexico?
choices: A job in a factory that makes plants
A temporary job on a project basis
A position on the ground floor
questions.explanation: De planta means permanent: a job on the company's permanent staff, usually with benefits (las prestaciones). Freelancers (trabajadores independientes) work by project instead.

questions.stem: Which of these markers belong mainly to informal speech? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: O sea, encima and total (like para colmo and en fin) are colloquial; in a formal text they sound careless. En cualquier caso is neutral to formal, and dicho de otro modo is if anything a little formal.

questions.stem: Complete with a two-word marker that means "by the way": "___, ¿ya enviaste tu currículum?"
questions.explanation: Por cierto opens a side remark. A propósito (which you learned in A2 as "on purpose") can be used the same way, so it is accepted too.

questions.stem: Match each marker to its job.
choices: Giving the reason that settles it
questions.explanation: Es decir says the same thing another way; de hecho supports what was said with a fact; es más adds a weightier argument for the same side; por cierto digresses; al fin y al cabo gives the decisive reason. Ordering a list is the job of B1's en primer lugar or por último.

questions.stem: Name the jobs at the top of the numbered columns.

image.alt: The discourse-marker chart from the lesson with the five column headings hidden and numbered. Column 1: es decir, o sea, mejor dicho, dicho de otro modo. Column 2: de hecho, en realidad, más bien. Column 3: además, es más, encima, para colmo, with an arrow labeled más fuerte. Column 4: por cierto, a propósito. Column 5: al fin y al cabo, de todos modos, en cualquier caso, en fin, total.

questions.explanation: Column 1 says the same thing another way (reformular); column 2 corrects or nuances (corregir y matizar); column 3 adds and builds up, from neutral además to exasperated para colmo (añadir y reforzar); column 4 opens a side remark (hacer un paréntesis); column 5 closes or waves the topic away (concluir o restar importancia).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: In fact, they're the first thing I look at.
questions.explanation: "De hecho, son lo primero que reviso": de hecho backs up the previous point with a fact and takes a comma after it at the start of a sentence. Revisó is the él/ella preterite, not "I look at".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I missed the bus and, to top it all off, it started to rain.
questions.explanation: "Perdí el camión y, para colmo, empezó a llover": para colmo marks the last straw and sits between commas after y. Perdió would mean that someone else missed the bus.

questions.stem: Which sentence says the same thing as "La reducción del consumo de azúcar provocó una disminución de la presión arterial"?
choices: They reduced the sugar in the blood, and people consumed less.
People ate less sugar, and as a result their blood pressure went down.
Blood pressure went down, so people ate less sugar.
People ate more sugar, but their blood pressure didn't change.
questions.explanation: Unpack the nouns: la reducción del consumo = people consumed less; provocó = caused; una disminución de la presión = blood pressure went down. The cause is eating less sugar, and the effect is lower blood pressure, not the other way around.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ análisis de los datos tardó tres meses."
questions.explanation: Análisis is masculine, though it ends in -is: el análisis. The plural doesn't change (los análisis), but tardó is singular here, so el. Lo is the neuter article, used with adjectives, not nouns.

questions.stem: Which is the noun from "mejorar" used in "la ___ de la calidad"?
questions.explanation: The noun is la mejora, with no suffix. Mejoración, mejoranza and mejoraje follow real suffix patterns but don't exist: nominalizations have to be learned or looked up, not built by rule.

questions.stem: A survey found that students who use their phones more at night sleep less. Which sentence reports it correctly?
choices: Los datos demuestran que el celular causa insomnio.
El estudio prueba que el celular es la causa.
Los datos sugieren una relación entre el uso del celular y el sueño.
El celular provocó que todos durmieran menos.
questions.explanation: An observational study shows a correlation, not a cause, so a careful writer hedges: los datos sugieren una relación. Demuestran, prueba and provocó all claim a cause that the data can't establish.

questions.stem: What does "lo ocurrido" mean in "La empresa pidió disculpas por lo ocurrido"?
questions.explanation: Lo + participle names the thing that was done: lo ocurrido = what happened (like lo dicho, what was said). It refers to a past event, not a future one, a person or a place.

questions.stem: Which verb completes the support-verb phrase? "Antes de ___ una decisión, necesitamos más datos."
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is tomar una decisión (to make a decision). Hacer una decisión is a calque of English, and realizar or dar don't combine with decisión.

questions.stem: What does "No hay pruebas de que el celular cause insomnio" mean?
choices: There are no tests for phone insomnia.
There's no evidence that phones cause insomnia.
Phones don't cause insomnia in tests.
There's no proof that insomnia damages phones.
questions.explanation: Here la prueba (A1: test) has its other sense, evidence or proof. The sentence says nothing about medical tests and keeps the direction: phones → insomnia.

questions.stem: Which of these nouns are feminine? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Nouns in -ción, -anza and -dad are feminine: la comprobación, la enseñanza, la posibilidad. Nouns in -miento and -aje are masculine (el conocimiento, el aprendizaje), and so is el análisis.

questions.stem: Make it nominal. "Los investigadores observaron el fenómeno durante un año" → "La ___ del fenómeno duró un año."
questions.explanation: Observar becomes la observación (-ción, feminine, which agrees with la). The verb becomes a noun, and the time phrase moves into the main verb, duró.

questions.stem: Write in the missing nouns: choose the noun for each numbered row.

image.alt: The verb-to-noun chart from the lesson with five nouns and endings hidden and numbered. Row 1: mejorar. Row 2: analizar. Row 3 is visible: comprobar, la comprobación. Row 4: conocer. Row 5 is visible: financiar, el financiamiento. Row 6 is visible: observar, la observación. Row 7: aprender. Row 8: enseñar. Feminine rows are pink and masculine rows blue.

questions.explanation: mejorar → la mejora; analizar → el análisis; conocer → el conocimiento; aprender → el aprendizaje; enseñar → la enseñanza. The colors give the gender: pink rows are feminine, blue rows masculine. El aprendimiento and la enseñación don't exist.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Three hundred samples were analyzed.
questions.explanation: "Se analizaron trescientas muestras": the passive se agrees with the plural subject, muestras, so the verb is plural. "Trescientas muestras se analizaron" is also correct. With analizó, the agreement the DPD recommends is lost.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The data suggest that sleep improves memory.
questions.explanation: "Los datos sugieren que el sueño mejora la memoria": los datos is plural, so sugieren. Sugerir que + indicative reports what the data indicate; the hedge is in the verb sugieren, not demuestran.

questions.stem: Match each support-verb phrase to the simple verb it replaces.
questions.explanation: In each phrase the support verb carries the tense and the noun carries the meaning: un estudio → estudiar, un análisis → analizar, una decisión → decidir, una explicación → explicar. Preguntar would be hacer una pregunta.

questions.stem: "El 40 % de los encuestados ___ que el servicio es malo." Which verb form is correct?
questions.explanation: With a percentage + de + a plural noun, the verb can agree with the percentage (opina) or with the noun (opinan). The DPD accepts both and notes that the plural is generally more frequent.

questions.stem: Complete: "La mayoría de los encuestados ___ satisfechos con el transporte."
questions.explanation: When the verb has an adjective describing the subject (satisfechos), only the plural sounds normal: la mayoría de los encuestados están satisfechos. Está would clash with the plural adjective, and satisfecho goes with estar, not ser.

questions.stem: A share went from 20% to 25%. How do you describe the change precisely?
questions.explanation: From 20 to 25 is five percentage points (and, relative to the start, a 25% increase). "Un 5 %" confuses points with percent; it didn't double (that would be 40%), and it didn't fall.

questions.stem: What does "Las ventas en línea se triplicaron" mean?
choices: Online sales fell by a third.
Online sales were divided into three.
Online sales rose by three percent.
questions.explanation: Triplicarse means to become three times as large. A third is un tercio, and three percent would be un 3 %.

questions.stem: "Tres de cada diez jóvenes viven solos." What percentage is that?
questions.explanation: Tres de cada diez = three out of ten = 30%. Notice the plural verb: the subject is tres.

questions.stem: Which way of writing 126 million (126,014,024) does the DPD recommend?
questions.explanation: The DPD recommends grouping digits in threes with a space, not a point or a comma, which avoids confusion between countries that use the point or the comma for decimals. Everyday Mexican writing often uses commas (126,014,024), but INEGI's reports use spaces.

questions.stem: Which sentence makes a polite request in a formal e-mail?
choices: Estudie ya la posibilidad de construir departamentos.
Le agradecería que estudiara la posibilidad de construir departamentos.
Encima, quiero que estudia la posibilidad de construir departamentos.
Total, que estudien la posibilidad de construir departamentos.
questions.explanation: Le agradecería que + imperfect subjunctive is the safe formal request. A bare command sounds rude in a formal letter; encima and total are colloquial, and quiero que needs the subjunctive (estudie), not estudia.

questions.stem: Which of these describe a figure going down? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Descender, disminuir and registrar un descenso all describe a fall. Incrementarse and duplicarse describe a rise, and mantenerse estable means it stayed the same.

questions.stem: Complete with one verb in the preterite: "El porcentaje ___ del 7 % al 14 %." (It went from 7% to 14%.)
questions.explanation: The lesson's pattern is pasar de… a…: pasó del 7 % al 14 %. Any verb of rising also works with del… al…: subió, aumentó, creció, se incrementó. Note del and al: de + el, a + el.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this formal e-mail.

image.alt: The formal e-mail from the lesson with seven blocks and no labels; six blocks are numbered. A visible first block reads Asunto: Datos de la encuesta Vivir en San Andrés y una propuesta. 1: Estimada licenciada Herrera: 2: Me dirijo a usted como vecina del municipio para hacerle llegar algunos datos… 3: Según la encuesta Vivir en San Andrés 2026, el 14 % de los jóvenes de 18 a 34 años viven solos… 4: Desde mi punto de vista, estas cifras muestran que la oferta actual no responde a la demanda… 5: Por ello, le agradecería que la Dirección estudiara la posibilidad de incluir departamentos… 6: Quedo a su disposición para cualquier aclaración. Atentamente, Mariana Solís Treviño.

questions.explanation: A formal e-mail moves from greeting (with a colon) to purpose (me dirijo a usted para…), data (según la encuesta…), opinion (desde mi punto de vista…), request (le agradecería que…) and closing (quedo a su disposición… atentamente). El remitente is the sender, which appears in the From line, not in the body.

questions.stem: Match each trend expression to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Duplicarse ×2, triplicarse ×3; mantenerse estable = no change; registrar un descenso = to show a fall; alcanzar (el 30 %) = to reach. To halve is reducirse a la mitad.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Most of the respondents are satisfied.
questions.explanation: "La mayoría de los encuestados están satisfechos": with an adjective (satisfechos) describing the subject, the plural verb is the norm (the less usual verb-first order, Están satisfechos la mayoría de los encuestados, is also accepted). Está would not agree with satisfechos.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Sales rose 10% compared to the previous year.
questions.explanation: "Las ventas subieron un 10 % respecto al año anterior." The comparison can also open the sentence (Respecto al año anterior, las ventas subieron un 10 %), and the verb can come first (Subieron las ventas un 10 %…). Subió would not agree with las ventas.

questions.stem: Complete the proposal: "Yo propondría que el municipio ___ en reparar las fugas."
questions.explanation: A proposal softened with the conditional (propondría) is usually followed by the imperfect subjunctive: invirtiera (invertir, like sentir: invirtieron → invirtiera). The indicative invierte and the conditional invertiría can't follow que here, and the infinitive needs no que. (The present subjunctive invierta is also heard in Latin America; the imperfect is the safe choice.)

questions.stem: You accept a fact: "Estoy de acuerdo en que el agua ___ el problema principal."
questions.explanation: Estar de acuerdo en que + indicative accepts something as a fact: el agua es el problema principal. In the negative (No estoy de acuerdo en que…), the subjunctive sea would be usual.

questions.stem: Complete: "No es que las pipas ___ malas, es que no resuelven nada."
questions.explanation: No es que rejects an interpretation and takes the subjunctive (sean); the real reason after es que is in the indicative (resuelven).

questions.stem: Complete: "Habría que ___ más pipas para los días sin servicio."
questions.explanation: Habría que (one would have to, we'd need to) is followed by an infinitive: habría que pedir. It has no subject, so there's no que + subjunctive.

questions.stem: "La campaña fue eficaz, pero no eficiente." What does it mean?
choices: It achieved its effect, but it was costly or wasteful.
It was cheap, but it didn't work.
It didn't work, and it was expensive.
It worked well and cost little.
questions.explanation: Eficaz = it achieves its effect; eficiente (B1) = it does so without waste. Effective but not efficient: it worked, at a high cost.

questions.stem: "Las pipas son una solución a corto plazo." What does a corto plazo mean?
questions.explanation: A corto plazo = in the short term; a largo plazo = in the long term. El plazo is a period of time or a deadline.

questions.stem: Complete the refutation: "Es cierto que la campaña costó poco; eso no quiere decir que ___."
questions.explanation: Eso no quiere decir que + subjunctive rejects a conclusion: haya funcionado (perfect subjunctive: that it has worked). A gerund, a bare participle or an infinitive can't follow que.

questions.stem: Which of these introduce a proposal? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Yo propondría que, Lo ideal sería que and Habría que put forward what should be done. Es cierto que concedes a point, and Eso no quiere decir que refutes a conclusion.

questions.stem: Complete with the imperfect subjunctive of empezar: "Sería conveniente que la campaña ___ antes del verano."
questions.explanation: Sería conveniente que (conditional) + imperfect subjunctive: empezara (from empezaron). The -se form, empezase, is also correct.

questions.stem: Mexico says concientizar (to raise awareness). Which verb does Spain usually use?
questions.explanation: Spain says concienciar and la concienciación; Mexico and much of Latin America say concientizar and la concientización. Both are in the DLE.

questions.stem: Match each phrase to what it does in a debate.
left: Si entiendo bien, usted propone que…
questions.explanation: A good refutation sums up the other argument fairly, concedes what is reasonable, rebuts with a counterargument and proposes something better. Opening a side remark is por cierto's job (lesson 17).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'd propose that the municipality invest in the network.
questions.explanation: "Yo propondría que el municipio invirtiera en la red": conditional + imperfect subjunctive. Yo can be left out or follow propondría, and the subject can follow the verb (que invirtiera el municipio en la red). Invierte, an indicative, can't follow propondría que.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: That doesn't mean it can't be done.
questions.explanation: "Eso no quiere decir que no se pueda hacer": eso no quiere decir que takes the subjunctive (se pueda). The indicative no se puede doesn't fit after it.

questions.stem: A student copies the source's sentences in the same order, swaps a few words for synonyms and gives no reference. What is it?
questions.explanation: Changing a few words doesn't make the text yours: same sentences, same order and no reference is plagiarism (el plagio). A real paraphrase changes the structure and still cites the source; a quotation uses quotation marks and a reference.

questions.stem: "Ferrer advierte que la peatonalización puede expulsar a los negocios tradicionales." What does advierte tell you?
questions.explanation: Advertir que = to warn that. The reporting verb shows the author's stance; denying would be negar, raising a question plantear.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ferrer propone que se ___ también en los vecinos."
questions.explanation: Proponer que reports an influence (what should happen), so it takes the subjunctive: se piense. Statements reported with afirma, señala or sostiene take the indicative.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ferrer sostiene que la ciudad caminable ___ una cuestión de justicia social."
questions.explanation: Sostener que (to maintain, to argue) reports a statement, so the indicative follows: es.

questions.stem: Which quotation marks does the RAE recommend first in printed texts?
questions.explanation: The RAE recommends angle quotes « » first in printed texts, then double and single quotes for quotations inside quotations. In Mexico double quotes are far more common; either is fine if used consistently.

questions.stem: You paraphrase an idea in your own words and structure. Do you need a reference?
choices: No, because the words are yours.
Only if the paraphrase is longer than 40 words.
Only in a bibliography, never in the text.
Yes, because the idea comes from the source.
questions.explanation: A paraphrase changes the words, not the owner of the idea: it needs a reference in the text and an entry in the list at the end.

questions.stem: What is "el resumen ejecutivo" of a report?
choices: A short summary at the start for decision makers
The list of works cited at the end
A note at the bottom of a page
questions.explanation: El resumen ejecutivo states the problem, the findings and the recommendation in a page or less, so that a busy reader can stop there. The list of works is la bibliografía, the table of contents el índice, and a note at the bottom la nota al pie.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the plural of modesty?
choices: En este trabajo se analizan tres casos.
En este trabajo analizo tres casos.
En este trabajo analizamos tres casos.
En este trabajo analizaron tres casos.
questions.explanation: The plural of modesty is one author writing nosotros: analizamos. Se analizan is the impersonal alternative; analizo uses yo, which academic Spanish usually avoids; analizaron refers to other people.

questions.stem: A paper uses Chicago style. Where does the full reference to a source usually appear the first time it is cited?
choices: Nowhere: only the year is given
questions.explanation: Chicago style typically gives the full reference in a footnote (una nota al pie) the first time and a short form after that; APA uses author and year in the text. Whatever the style, use one consistently.

questions.stem: Complete with the infinitive that means "to put in one's own words": "Hay que ___ la idea y citar la fuente."
questions.explanation: Parafrasear is a regular -ear verb (parafraseo, parafraseé). The noun is la paráfrasis.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this student paper.

image.alt: Three pages of a student paper with five numbered markers. 1 is beside the heading Índice on page 1, above a list of chapters with page numbers. 2 is at the right end of a highlighted sentence in quotation marks with a small raised 1 on page 2. 3 is at the right of the last paragraph of page 2. 4 is on a note at the bottom of page 2, below a short line, that begins 1 L. Ferrer. 5 is beside the heading Bibliografía on page 3, above three entries in alphabetical order.

questions.explanation: The table of contents (el índice) opens the paper; the quotation in quotation marks is la cita textual; the last paragraph is el párrafo de cierre; the numbered note at the foot of the page is la nota al pie; the alphabetical list at the end is la bibliografía.

questions.stem: When they report a statement, which of these are followed by the indicative? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Afirma, señala, sostiene and advierte report statements, so the indicative follows (afirma que es…). Propone que reports an influence and takes the subjunctive (propone que se piense…).

questions.stem: Match each reporting verb to its nuance.
questions.explanation: Choosing the verb tells the reader how the author makes the claim. "Denies" would be niega.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Ferrer argues that cities are changing.
questions.explanation: "Ferrer sostiene que las ciudades están cambiando": sostener que + indicative. The verb can also come first, as in formal writing: "Sostiene Ferrer que…". Estén (subjunctive) doesn't fit after a verb that reports a statement.

questions.stem: "I'm going to a design conference in Guadalajara." Which is right?
choices: Voy a una conferencia de diseño en Guadalajara.
Voy a un congreso de diseño en Guadalajara.
Voy a una ponencia de diseño en Guadalajara.
Voy a un discurso de diseño en Guadalajara.
questions.explanation: The event is un congreso. Una conferencia is a single lecture, una ponencia a talk given at the congress, and un discurso a speech.

questions.stem: According to the talk, when did the Mexico City Metro open?
questions.explanation: The speaker says el 4 de septiembre de 1969, with the first stretch of Line 1 between Zaragoza and Chapultepec. In a note it would be 4/9/1969, day first. 1968 was the year of the Olympic Games.

questions.stem: Why is Chapultepec's pictogram a grasshopper, according to the speaker?
choices: Because grasshoppers were sold at the station
Because it was the Olympic mascot
Because it translates the Nahuatl name, usually rendered as "hill of the grasshopper"
questions.explanation: The speaker says the name, of Nahuatl origin, is usually translated as cerro del chapulín, so the drawing translates the name. Nothing in the talk mentions selling grasshoppers or a mascot.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the idea that the pictograms were made for people who couldn't read?
choices: It is partly true, but the drawings helped everyone, not only people who couldn't read.
It is the official reason given by the Metro in 1969.
It is false, because everyone could read in 1969.
questions.explanation: In her digression she calls it una idea muy extendida that tiene parte de verdad (part of the population couldn't read in 1969), but adds that the pictograms weren't only for them, since a drawing is recognized faster than a name. She doesn't call it false or the official reason.

questions.stem: A speaker says "Abro un paréntesis." What comes next?
questions.explanation: Abrir un paréntesis announces a digression, closed later with cierro el paréntesis. What comes between is rarely the main point.

questions.stem: In Spanish notes, what does "xq" stand for?
