questions.explanation: xq is short for porque. Que is q, por ejemplo ej., aproximadamente aprox.

questions.stem: Choose the yo preterite of exponer: "En el congreso ___ mis resultados."
questions.explanation: Exponer goes like poner: puse → expuse, with no written accent. Exponí follows the regular -er pattern, which this verb doesn't use.

questions.stem: Which of these would be out of place in a short acceptance speech?
choices: A ten-minute list of every source you used
Thanking the people behind the work
questions.explanation: An acceptance speech is short (under a minute): thanks, the people behind the work, a dedication, thanks again. A list of sources belongs in a paper's bibliography.

questions.stem: Put the parts of a lecture in the order the lesson gives.
choices: Anuncio del tema y del plan
questions.explanation: A talk greets, announces its plan, develops its points, concludes and then opens the floor to questions (el turno de preguntas).

questions.stem: Complete with the preterite of exponer: "La investigadora ___ sus resultados en el congreso."
questions.explanation: Exponer goes like poner: puso → expuso.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in this conference room.

image.alt: The conference room from the lesson with five numbered markers: 1 beside the woman speaking on the stage; 2 at the top right of the large screen showing Pictogramas del Metro and a bar chart; 3 on the wooden stand in front of the woman; 4 beside the small black object on a stalk in front of her face; 5 on the rows of seated people seen from behind.

questions.explanation: The woman giving the talk is la ponente; the screen shows una diapositiva; she stands behind el atril (the lectern) and speaks into el micrófono; the audience in their seats is el auditorio, a word that also names the room.

questions.stem: Match each signpost to its job in a talk.
questions.explanation: These are the moments to write a new heading in your notes. Announcing the plan sounds like Mi ponencia tiene tres partes… En primer lugar…

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Today I'm going to talk to you about the Metro's pictograms.
questions.explanation: "Hoy voy a hablarles de los pictogramas del Metro": ir a + infinitive with the pronoun attached (hablarles, to you all). Hoy can also follow hablarles or close the sentence. The gerund hablándoles doesn't follow voy a.

questions.stem: What is "el sacapuntas"?
questions.explanation: Saca (pulls out, here: sharpens to a point) + puntas (points): a pencil sharpener. A corkscrew is el sacacorchos, a can opener el abrelatas, and nail clippers el cortaúñas.

questions.stem: Complete: "En la cocina hay dos ___."
questions.explanation: Verb + plural noun compounds keep the same form in the plural: un abrelatas, dos abrelatas. The singular already ends in -s, so nothing is added.

questions.stem: Which word means "useless"?
questions.explanation: The prefix in- means "not": útil → inútil. Des- undoes an action (hacer → deshacer), anti- means against and sub- under; none of them forms an adjective from útil.

questions.stem: "Se fue enojada y dio un portazo." What did she do?
choices: She fixed the door before leaving.
questions.explanation: La puerta + -azo = el portazo, the slam of a door: -azo names a blow or a sudden, forceful act. Dar un portazo = to slam the door.

questions.stem: —¿Ya lavaste los trastes? —Ahorita los lavo. What does the second speaker mean?
choices: I washed them a little while ago.
I'll wash them in a moment.
questions.explanation: With a present verb about the near future, ahorita means "in a moment" (or "soon"). "A little while ago" would need a past tense (Ahorita los lavé). Its exact sense depends on context and tone, but nothing here says "never" or "every day".

questions.stem: In Mexico, what do you use "un desarmador" for?
choices: to put in and take out screws
to make holes in a wall
questions.explanation: El desarmador (from desarmar, to take apart) is the Mexican word for a screwdriver; Spain says el destornillador. A bottle opener is el destapador, a drill el taladro, a mop el trapeador.

questions.stem: Write the -ito diminutive of "poco" (mind the spelling): "Espérame un ___."
questions.explanation: Poco → poquito: the c becomes qu before i to keep the k sound, like amigo → amiguito (g → gu) and taza → tacita (z → c). The double diminutive poquitito (a tiny bit) is also heard.

questions.stem: Match each suffix with what it usually makes.
choices: a blow or a sudden act
a person who does something too much
questions.explanation: Lavable = that can be washed; la zapatería = the shoe shop; el portazo = the slam of a door; seguro → la seguridad. A person who does something too much takes -ón (llorón, mandón), which isn't in the list.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things.

image.alt: A toolbox with a bucket beside it, and six numbered things: a hammer, a screwdriver, a power drill, a nail, a screw and the bucket.

questions.explanation: El martillo (hammer), el desarmador (screwdriver, Mexico), el taladro (power drill), el clavo (nail: smooth), el tornillo (screw: with a thread) and la cubeta (bucket, Mexico). There is no mop (el trapeador) or hose (la manguera) in the picture.

questions.stem: Build the question in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Can you lend me the screwdriver? (tú, Mexico)
questions.explanation: "¿Me prestas el desarmador?" El desarmador is the Mexican screwdriver; el destapador is a bottle opener. The pronoun me goes before the conjugated verb.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The umbrellas are in the car.
questions.explanation: "Los paraguas están en el carro" (or "En el carro están los paraguas", with the subject after the verb). El paraguas is masculine, like every verb + noun compound, even though las aguas is feminine, and its plural doesn't change.

questions.stem: Which of these nouns keep the same form in the plural? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Verb + plural noun compounds don't change: los sacacorchos, los rascacielos, los parabrisas. El cucharón is an augmentative (los cucharones) and la manguera an ordinary noun (las mangueras).

questions.stem: Complete: "Muchas gracias ___ la visita guiada."
questions.explanation: You thank someone for a cause: gracias por. "Gracias para" is a common learner mistake: para looks at a goal, not a reason.

questions.stem: Complete with the deadline meaning (no later than Friday): "Tenemos que reservar ___ el viernes."
questions.explanation: A deadline takes para: para el viernes = by Friday. Desde (since) and durante (during) don't give a deadline, and por with a day points to a rough time, not a limit.

questions.stem: "Trabajo por mi familia." What does it mean?
choices: I work for my family's sake.
I work at my family's house.
I work in order to meet my family.
questions.explanation: Por gives the cause or the person on whose behalf you act: I work for my family's sake. "My family employs me" would be Trabajo para mi familia (employer); "at my family's house" would be en casa de mi familia.

questions.stem: "Quedan tres kilómetros por recorrer." What does the guide mean?
choices: We have already walked three kilometers.
Three kilometers were walked by the group.
We are three kilometers from the start.
There are still three kilometers to go.
questions.explanation: Quedar + por + infinitive = still to be done: three kilometers still to be covered. The past distance would be Ya recorrimos tres kilómetros.

questions.stem: "Para ser temporada seca, hay mucha agua en la laguna." What does "para ser temporada seca" mean?
choices: in order to be the dry season
questions.explanation: Para + ser compares with what you'd expect: for the dry season (considering it is the dry season), there's a lot of water. It isn't a purpose or a cause here.

questions.stem: Which question asks specifically about the purpose (what for)?
questions.explanation: ¿Para qué? asks about the goal (what for?); ¿por qué? asks about the cause (why?). In conversation people often answer ¿por qué? with a purpose too, but only ¿para qué? asks for one.

questions.stem: Complete the fixed phrase: "Lleva impermeable, por si ___."
questions.explanation: Por si acaso = just in case. Por si can also take a clause in the indicative: por si llueve.

questions.stem: Complete with por or para: "Pasamos ___ Oaxaca de camino a Chiapas."
questions.explanation: Por gives the route you go through: pasar por Oaxaca = to go through (or by) Oaxaca. The destination, Chiapas, could take para: salimos para Chiapas.

questions.stem: Match each sentence with the use of por or para in it.
left: Cerraron el sendero por la lluvia.
questions.explanation: Por la lluvia gives the cause; para el lunes, a deadline; por 90 pesos, an exchange; para ver aves, a purpose. None of the sentences is a passive, so "agent" matches nothing.

questions.stem: Name the numbered places on this map of an invented park.

image.alt: A map of an invented coastal park with six numbered places: a dashed trail through the forest, a tower on a hill, a round pool of water, trees around a lagoon, the sand along the coast, and corals in the sea.

questions.explanation: The dashed line is el sendero (trail, lesson 08); the tower on the hill, el mirador (viewpoint, A2); the round pool, el cenote; the trees around the lagoon, el manglar; the corals in the sea, el arrecife; the sand, la playa. There is no waterfall (la cascada) or crater (el cráter).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: We walked along the riverbank.
questions.explanation: "Caminamos por la orilla del río." Por gives the route (along, through). "Caminamos para la orilla" would mean toward the bank, a different sentence.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Bring a cap, just in case. (tú)
questions.explanation: "Lleva gorra, por si acaso" (or "Por si acaso, lleva gorra"). Por si acaso is a fixed phrase: it never takes para.

questions.stem: Which greeting is right for a formal letter in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A formal letter opens with Estimado / Estimada + title + name, followed by a colon. A comma after the greeting is English punctuation; Hola is informal; Querida with a bare surname mixes registers.

questions.stem: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: La propuesta del ayuntamiento, me parece excelente.
La propuesta del ayuntamiento me parece excelente.
La propuesta, del ayuntamiento me parece excelente.
La propuesta del ayuntamiento me parece, excelente.
questions.explanation: No comma goes between a subject (la propuesta del ayuntamiento) and its verb (me parece), however long the subject is. The other commas split a phrase or separate the verb from its complement.

questions.stem: Which is written correctly?
choices: La reunión es el Lunes 3 de Septiembre.
La reunión es el lunes 3 de Septiembre.
La reunión es el Lunes 3 de septiembre.
La reunión es el lunes 3 de septiembre.
questions.explanation: In Spanish, days of the week and months are written in lowercase: el lunes 3 de septiembre.

questions.stem: What should the conclusion of an opinion article do?
choices: Repeat the introduction word for word.
Sum up the position or make a proposal.
questions.explanation: La conclusión sums up (sintetiza) your position or proposes something; it doesn't add new arguments, and repeating the introduction word for word is reiteration.

questions.stem: According to the official guide, how long is each DELE B2 writing task?
questions.explanation: Each of the two tasks asks for 150 to 180 words, 300 to 360 in all. 200–250 words is the length of the input recording or news item, not of your text.

questions.stem: Rosa Elena has already written "la propuesta" twice. Which word lets her refer to it again without reiteration?
questions.explanation: La iniciativa (or la medida) is a synonym that refers to the same proposal. La conclusión, la errata and la posdata name other things.

questions.stem: In "La idea es buena; sin embargo, llega tarde", the sign after "buena" is el ___.
questions.explanation: El punto y coma (semicolon) joins two closely linked sentences, often before a connector like sin embargo. Its plural doesn't change: los punto y coma.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: However, I am worried about access.
questions.explanation: "Sin embargo, me preocupa el acceso." Preocupar works like gustar: the thing that worries (el acceso) is the subject, so the verb is preocupa, with me for the person. "Me preocupo" would be reflexive (I worry).

questions.stem: Put the parts of a formal letter in order.
choices: Me dirijo a ustedes en relación con la propuesta del ayuntamiento.
En primer lugar, quisiera expresar mi apoyo a la iniciativa.
Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.
questions.explanation: Greeting with a colon; the opening line that says why you write; the body; the closing sentence; the sign-off, followed by your name.

questions.stem: Match each part of a text with its job.
choices: presents the topic and the thesis
gives the main ideas, one per paragraph
supports a main idea with an example or data
questions.explanation: Introduction, body (desarrollo), conclusion; ideas secundarias support each idea principal. A typing mistake is una errata, which isn't in the list.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I am writing to you about the proposal. (formal, to several people)
questions.explanation: "Me dirijo a ustedes en relación con la propuesta": the standard opening of a formal letter. The phrase is en relación con (also con relación a).

questions.stem: Which of these are written with a lowercase initial in the middle of a Spanish sentence? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Days, months, languages and nationalities take lowercase in Spanish: el lunes, octubre, el francés. Place names are proper names: Guadalajara.

questions.stem: What do you need to get "Apto" in the DELE B2?
choices: at least 30 of 50 points in each of the two groups
at least 15 points in each of the four tests
a pass in writing and speaking only
questions.explanation: The 100 points form two groups of 50 (reading + writing, listening + speaking), and each group needs at least 30. A total of 60 isn't enough if one group is under 30.

questions.stem: How many times is each recording played in the listening test?
choices: as many times as you like
questions.explanation: Every recording in the listening test is played twice, so you can get the main idea first and check details the second time.

questions.stem: Which test has four tasks and 36 items?
questions.explanation: Reading: 70 minutes, 4 tasks, 36 items. Listening has 5 tasks and 30 items; writing has 2 tasks; speaking has 3.

questions.stem: What happens if you choose a wrong answer in the reading test?
questions.explanation: There is no penalización: each correct item scores 1 (the total is converted to the test's 25 points) and a wrong one costs nothing, so never leave an item blank.

questions.stem: A candidate writes and speaks Mexican Spanish consistently. What does the guide say?
choices: It is accepted: any educated norm used consistently is.
Mexican words lose points in writing.
questions.explanation: The guide accepts any Hispanic norm applied consistently and backed by large groups of educated speakers. What loses marks is mixing norms.

questions.stem: Complete: "Me dolió que no me lo ___ antes."
questions.explanation: A past main verb of feeling (me dolió que) needs the subjunctive, and for something earlier than it, the pluperfect subjunctive: hubieras dicho (or hubieses dicho). The other three are indicative or conditional forms, which this trigger doesn't take.

questions.stem: Complete: "Si hubiera estudiado medicina, ahora ___ médica."
questions.explanation: A mixed condition: a past cause (si hubiera estudiado) with a present result (ahora), so the result is the simple conditional: sería. Habría sido would put the result in the past, which clashes with ahora.

questions.stem: "Lo he visto", dijo Ana. Report it: "Ana dijo que lo ___ visto."
questions.explanation: After a past reporting verb, a perfect (or preterite) in direct speech becomes the pluperfect: había visto. Habría visto would be a guess or a condition; haya is subjunctive; hubo visto is the literary pretérito anterior.

questions.stem: The DELE B2 writing test lasts ___ minutes. (Write the number.)
questions.explanation: Writing: 80 minutes for two tasks of 150–180 words each. Reading lasts 70, listening 40, and speaking 20, after 20 minutes of preparation.

questions.stem: Complete with a form of haber: "Si hubiera salido antes, no ___ perdido el vuelo."
questions.explanation: The result of a past condition takes the conditional perfect, habría perdido. Hubiera perdido is also correct in the result, and very common in the Americas. Hubiese perdido is accepted too (the DPD allows it in this clause), but use habría or hubiera.

questions.stem: Match each DELE B2 test with its time.
questions.explanation: Reading 70, listening 40, writing 80, speaking 20 minutes after 20 minutes of preparation. No test lasts 60 minutes.

questions.stem: Which mood does each connector take?
choices: either, with a change of meaning
questions.explanation: Para que (purpose) and antes de que always take the subjunctive; ya que (cause) takes the indicative; aunque takes the indicative for a fact and the subjunctive for a possibility or a point you grant.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I hope you have passed. (tú)
questions.explanation: "Espero que hayas aprobado." Esperar que takes the subjunctive, and for something already done, the perfect subjunctive (lesson 02). "Has aprobado" is indicative.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Each recording is heard twice.
questions.explanation: "Cada audición se escucha dos veces" (or "Se escucha dos veces cada audición"). The passive se agrees with its singular subject, cada audición: se escucha, not se escuchan.

questions.stem: An Argentine friend says "¿Vos tenés tiempo?" How would a Mexican ask the same?
questions.explanation: Vos tenés = tú tienes. In the vos form the stress moves to the ending and the stem change disappears (tenés, not tienés).

questions.stem: Which is the Río de la Plata command of venir (to vos)?
questions.explanation: A vos command drops the -r of the infinitive and stresses the last vowel: venir → vení, decir → decí, hablar → hablá. Venga is the usted command.

questions.stem: In voseo, how do you say "with you" (to one friend)?
questions.explanation: Vos is used after prepositions: con vos, para vos. There is no special form like the tú speaker's contigo.

questions.stem: A Costa Rican mother calls her son "usted". What does it usually show?
choices: the normal, warm address in many Costa Rican families
that she doesn't know him well
questions.explanation: In Costa Rica usted reaches almost every situation, family and friends included, so it isn't a sign of distance there (Calderón Campos, 2010).

questions.stem: What is typical of Chilean familiar speech, according to the DPD?
choices: the pronoun vos with tú verb forms
the pronoun tú with vos-type verb endings (tú sabís)
questions.explanation: Many Chileans say tú with voseo endings in familiar speech (¿Tú sabís?); the pronoun vos itself is avoided in educated speech there, and more careful speech uses ordinary tú forms.

questions.stem: "Hace mucho frío en Buenos Aires, ¿viste?" What does "¿viste?" do here?
choices: It asks if you saw the city.
It works like "you know?" at the end of a sentence.
It asks you to look at something.
questions.explanation: ¿Viste? is a Río de la Plata tag, like "you know?" or "see?". Literally it is the preterite of ver, but here it doesn't ask about seeing.

questions.stem: What is el lunfardo?
questions.explanation: El lunfardo is the slang of Buenos Aires, usually traced to the late 19th and early 20th centuries; B1's laburar and el pibe come from it.

questions.stem: How do Argentines say "you all" to a group of friends?
questions.explanation: In all of the Americas the plural of address is ustedes, for friends and strangers alike. Vosotros is used in most of Spain.

questions.stem: Match each Río de la Plata form with the Mexican tú form.
questions.explanation: Ser: vos sos = tú eres. Tener: tenés = tienes. Commands: decí = di, sentate = siéntate. Vienes would match vos venís, which isn't in the list.

questions.stem: Rewrite in Mexican Spanish: "¿Vos querés venir?" → "¿Tú ___ venir?"
questions.explanation: Vos querés = tú quieres. The tú form keeps the stem change (quie-), which the vos form loses because its stress falls on the ending.

questions.stem: In educated Río de la Plata speech, which of these are the same for tú and vos? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Vos hablaste, te quiero, tu casa: the same as with tú. The present differs: vos hablás, tú hablas.

questions.stem: Build the question in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Do you want some mate? (Mexican Spanish, tú)
questions.explanation: "¿Quieres un mate?" is the Mexican tú form. Querés is the vos form you would hear in Buenos Aires; this course doesn't ask you to produce it.

questions.stem: What should your notes look like in the 20 minutes of preparation?
choices: the full text of what you'll say
questions.explanation: Notas de apoyo in key words: full sentences tempt you to read aloud, which sounds unnatural. The guide lets you use the notes and outline you made while preparing.

questions.stem: What does speaking task 2 ask you to do?
choices: Debate a law with the examiner.
Describe an imagined situation from a photo and talk about it.
questions.explanation: Task 2 (prepared) starts from a photo: you describe it, imagine the situation, and talk about it with the examiner.

questions.stem: Which statement about speaking task 3 is true?
choices: It has no preparation and starts from survey results or news.
questions.explanation: Task 3 isn't prepared: a short conversation, 3 to 4 minutes, about survey results or news on a current trend, chosen from two options.

questions.stem: You lose your place in the middle of your talk. Which phrase helps you pick up the thread?
questions.explanation: Como decía… (as I was saying) takes you back to your point. Mejor dicho rephrases; A ver and Es una buena pregunta buy time.

questions.stem: In her second draft, Lupe changed "En la radio dijeron que…" to "En la radio se dijo que…". Why?
choices: It's more formal, and the impersonal se fits a letter to an office.
questions.explanation: Both are correct Spanish; the impersonal se sounds more formal, which suits a letter to an institution (lesson 14).

questions.stem: Complete: "Las redes pueden informarnos, siempre y cuando no les ___ todo el trabajo."
questions.explanation: Siempre y cuando (as long as) always takes the subjunctive: dejemos. The indicative and conditional forms don't fit after it.

questions.stem: What is "la soltura"?
questions.explanation: La soltura is ease or fluency. A pause is la pausa, and an outline or concept map is el mapa conceptual.

questions.stem: In task 2, which sentence describes the background of the photo?
choices: Al fondo hay una pantalla de salidas.
Si yo estuviera en su lugar, buscaría un hotel.
Me imagino que tenía una reunión.
Bueno, el problema tiene tres caras.
questions.explanation: Al fondo (in the background) places something in the picture. The other sentences say what you would do, imagine a story, or open task 1.

questions.stem: Put Lupe's steps for writing task 1 in order.
choices: Make a plan of three paragraphs.
Revise it into a second draft.
questions.explanation: Notes from the recording come first, then the plan, the draft and the revision.

questions.stem: Match each phrase with its job in a conversation.
questions.explanation: Fillers like bueno and a ver buy time; mejor dicho rephrases; volviendo a lo de antes picks up the thread; entiendo lo que dice, pero… disagrees politely. None of them ends a conversation.

questions.stem: Complete with estar: "Si yo ___ en su lugar, buscaría otro vuelo."
questions.explanation: A hypothetical si clause about the present takes the imperfect subjunctive: si yo estuviera (or estuviese) en su lugar… + conditional.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I would combine the first two proposals.
questions.explanation: "Yo combinaría las dos primeras propuestas." A choice you are proposing takes the conditional (combinaría). Combinara is the imperfect subjunctive, used after si, not in the main clause.

questions.stem: How is the Golden Age of Mexican cinema usually dated?
questions.explanation: It is usually dated from 1936 (Allá en el Rancho Grande) to the mid-1950s, when television spread and several studios closed. 2014–2019 is when Mexican directors won five Oscars for best director.

questions.stem: What happened to Los olvidados after its premiere in December 1950?
choices: It won an Oscar the following year.
It was banned for twenty years.
It became the biggest box-office hit of the Golden Age.
It was pulled from theaters after a few days, then won best director at Cannes in 1951.
questions.explanation: The film caused an uproar and was pulled from Mexican theaters after a few days; the next year Buñuel won the award for best director at Cannes, and its reputation changed.

questions.stem: Roma came out in 2018. In which year did it win its Oscars?
questions.explanation: The Oscars are given early in the year after release, so Roma won at the 2019 ceremony: best director, best cinematography and best foreign-language film.

questions.stem: Who won the Oscar for best cinematography three years in a row (2014–2016)?
questions.explanation: Emmanuel Lubezki won for Gravity, Birdman and The Revenant. Gabriel Figueroa was the great cinematographer of the Golden Age.

questions.stem: Complete: "La película ___ en Veracruz."
questions.explanation: Se rodó: the preterite of rodar has no stem change (the stress falls on the ending), and the se passive agrees with la película (singular). Rueda, ruedo appear only where the stem is stressed.

questions.stem: Complete: "La serie fue ___ por una directora argentina."
questions.explanation: In the ser passive the participle agrees with the subject: la serie (feminine singular) → fue dirigida.

questions.stem: Complete: "Es la historia de una niña ___ padre se fue a trabajar al norte."
questions.explanation: Cuyo agrees with the thing possessed (padre, masculine singular), not with the owner (niña). "Que su padre" is heard in casual speech, but careful Spanish uses cuyo.

questions.stem: What is "un éxito de taquilla"?
questions.explanation: Un éxito de taquilla is a film that sells a lot of tickets (A2's la taquilla = box office).

questions.stem: Name the numbered things on this film set.

image.alt: A film set with five numbered things: a camera on a tripod, a boom microphone, a studio light, a clapperboard on a folding chair and a script on a table.

questions.explanation: La cámara on its tripod, el micrófono on the boom, el reflector (studio light), la claqueta (clapperboard) on the chair, and el guion (script, B1) on the table. There is no screen (la pantalla) or costume rack (el vestuario).

questions.stem: Match each word with its meaning.
choices: the person who writes the script
questions.explanation: Largo / corto + metraje: long and short films. La cartelera lists what's in theaters; el rodaje is the shooting. The person who writes the script is el guionista.

questions.stem: Write the yo present of rodar: "Los fines de semana, yo ___ cortometrajes con mi celular."
questions.explanation: Rodar changes o → ue when the stem is stressed: ruedo, ruedas, rueda, ruedan; but rodamos, and rodé in the preterite.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The film was nominated for five awards.
questions.explanation: "La película fue nominada a cinco premios" (or, putting the subject last, "Fue nominada a cinco premios la película"). Nominada agrees with la película; you are nominated a (for) an award.

Jalisco, 1917 – Mexico City, 1986. El llano en llamas (1953, stories) and Pedro Páramo (1955, novel).

Puebla, 1916 – Cuernavaca, 1998. Los recuerdos del porvenir (1963), La semana de colores (1964).
Master of the microrrelato; El dinosaurio, one sentence of seven words, in Obras completas (y otros cuentos), 1959.
Borges: Ficciones (1944), El Aleph (1949). Cortázar: "Casa tomada" (1946), in Bestiario (1951).

believable, plausible vs implausible. An invented story can be verosímil.

cards.front: la ambientación, la atmósfera, la intriga
cards.back: setting, mood, suspense: what makes a story work.
Time (map the tenses), narrator (who knows what), inference (clues → conclusion).
Conditional of probability in a narrative: He must have been about twenty.
essay; rehearsal (B1); trial (un ensayo clínico).

cards.front: Where does the name essay come from?
cards.back: Montaigne's Essais (1580): "attempts", a mind trying out an idea.
Monterrey, 1889 – Mexico City, 1959. Ateneo de la Juventud (1909); Visión de Anáhuac (1917).
First head of the SEP (1921–1924); La raza cósmica (1925), on mestizaje, much criticized today.
El laberinto de la soledad (1950): la mexicanidad and its máscaras. Nobel Prize in Literature, 1990.
Sobre cultura femenina (1950); Mujer que sabe latín… (1973). Ambassador to Israel, 1971–1974.
Hook → premise → examples → digression → objection answered → conclusion.
Esta es mi premisa… / Pensemos en… / Permítame una digresión… Vuelvo al tema. / Se dirá que… Es cierto, pero… / En conclusión…
to think over (reflexionar sobre algo) vs to reflect light, to show (reflejar).
to wait (esperar el tren), to hope (espero que llegue), to expect.

cards.front: When and how did muralism begin?
cards.back: 1921–1922: Vasconcelos at the SEP invited painters to cover public walls; San Ildefonso was the first great site.
Diego Rivera (1886–1957), José Clemente Orozco (1883–1949), David Alfaro Siqueiros (1896–1974).
Coyoacán, 1907–1954. Not a muralist: mostly small oils, many self-portraits; Las dos Fridas (1939).

cards.front: al fresco vs óleo sobre lienzo
cards.back: Pigment in water on wet plaster (part of the wall) vs oil paint on canvas (can be corrected).

cards.front: el pincel / la pincelada / el trazo
cards.back: brush / brushstroke / a line drawn with a pencil, pen or brush.
patron of the arts; same form in the plural and for a woman (los mecenas, la mecenas).
en primer plano, al fondo, en el centro, a la izquierda / derecha, en la parte superior / inferior.
se ve, aparece, se representa a…; fue pintado por…; la figura central, en torno a la cual…
parece simbolizar…, podría representar…, quizá aluda a…
Title, artist, date, technique and support, size, place: no verbs.
11 language families, 68 groupings (agrupaciones), 364 variants.
Published March 13, 2003: Indigenous languages and Spanish are lenguas nacionales with the same validity; it created INALI.
7,364,645 speakers of an Indigenous language aged 3 and over (about 6.1%). Most spoken: Nahuatl, 1,651,958.
náhuatl, maya, tseltal, tsotsil, mixteco, zapoteco.
A regional variety of one language. Don't call Indigenous languages dialectos: they are lenguas.

cards.front: lengua indígena / lengua originaria / lengua materna
cards.back: Indigenous language / native language of the Americas / mother tongue.
ahuacatl → aguacate, tomatl → tomate, mecatl → mecate, papalotl → papalote.
kite (Nahuatl papalotl, butterfly), turkey, peanut (Spain cacahuete).
In central Mexico: red tomato vs green tomatillo (often).
Words from Taíno, a Caribbean language, older in Spanish than the Nahuatl loans.
Yes, when the period is closed: Vivió veinte años en París. Compare the background: Cuando vivía en París, escribía todas las mañanas.

cards.front: Imperfect for a plan that didn't happen
cards.back: Iba a llamarte, pero se me acabó la batería (I was going to call you, but my battery died).
Quería pedirle un favor. Venía a preguntar si… The imperfect softens a request made now.

cards.front: Something finished today: Mexico vs Spain
cards.back: Mexico and most of Latin America: Hoy me levanté a las seis. Most of Spain: Hoy me he levantado a las seis. Both standard in their regions.
For what continues or repeats up to now and for "ever / not yet": He vivido aquí desde 2019; Últimamente he dormido mal; ¿Has estado en Oaxaca?
The preterite, in Mexico and in Spain: Falleció en 2009 (not ha fallecido en 2009).
The present tense for past events in biographies and timelines: En 1910 estalla la Revolución. Keep it consistent and give dates.

cards.front: en aquel entonces / a lo largo de / a raíz de
cards.back: back then (usually + imperfect) / throughout / as a result of, following

cards.front: la biografía / la autobiografía / las memorias
cards.back: written by someone else / the writer's own life / the writer's recollections of a period or of other people (plural in this sense)
Like conocer: fallezco, fallezca. Formal for morir: Falleció en su casa. El fallecimiento = the death (formal).
destaqué, evoqué (c → qu before e); subjunctive destaque, evoque
No written accent: me exilio, se exilia (regular -iar, like estudiar).
haya, hayas, haya, hayamos, hayan + participle: que hayas terminado. Pronouns before haya: que lo haya leído.
After a present, future or command main verb, for something already done: Espero que hayas aprobado; No creo que lo haya leído.

cards.front: No creo que estudie / No creo que haya estudiado
cards.back: I don't think he's studying or will study / I don't think he studied or has studied
When you've finished, let me know: finished before a future point. Cuando termines is also correct.
A relative clause about someone who may not exist, with a past description: Busco a alguien que haya hecho un posgrado.
Both moods: Es el mejor curso que he tomado / que haya tomado.
haya (of haber) and halla (of hallar, to find) sound the same; allá (over there) is stressed on the last syllable.
egresar = finish your coursework; titularse = complete every requirement and get the degree (often later)
Required work for the public before the degree; at the UNAM at least 480 hours over six months or more, starting with 70% of the credits.
Mexico: the oral exam before a panel (el jurado) that completes a degree, usually a thesis defense.
Mexico: the license to practice a profession, issued by the SEP's Dirección General de Profesiones.
tuition (Mexico; Spain las tasas) / grade average (Spain la nota media)

cards.front: el rector / la facultad / el catedrático
cards.back: university president (office: la rectoría) / school of a university / full professor (in Mexico often any university professor)
¡Felicidades! Me alegra que hayas aprobado. / Siento mucho que no hayas quedado.
hubiera, hubieras, hubiera, hubiéramos, hubieran + participle (-se: hubiese…, accepted)
After a past or conditional main verb, for an earlier event: Me dolió que no me hubieras invitado; Me habría gustado que me lo hubieras contado.

cards.front: Me dolió que no me invitaras
cards.back: Also correct: when the order is obvious, the imperfect subjunctive is common after a past main verb.
A regret about the past: Ojalá no le hubiera dicho nada (I wish I hadn't told him anything).
Ojalá venga (hope) / haya llegado (hope about the past) / estuviera aquí (unlikely now) / hubieras venido (regret)
Always a past subjunctive: como si fuera mi jefe (same time); como si no hubiera pasado nada (earlier).
Present, perfect, future, command → que vengas / que hayas venido. Past or conditional → que vinieras / que hubieras venido.

cards.front: No creo que lo dijera ayer
cards.back: Correct: a present main verb can take a past subjunctive for a past event.
to disappoint / to deceive, to cheat on (decepcionar is a false friend)
to be bitter after a wrong / to hold grudges by nature

cards.front: tener celos / darle celos a alguien
cards.back: to be jealous / to make someone jealous (los celos, usually plural)
Like sentir: hiero, hirió, hirieron, hiriendo, hiera, hiramos
to meet again: nos reencontramos, se reencuentran (o → ue like encontrar); el reencuentro = reunion
si + pluperfect subjunctive + conditional perfect: Si hubiera salido antes, no habría perdido el vuelo.
Very common, especially in the Americas, and accepted by the Nueva gramática: …no hubiera perdido el vuelo. Hubiese there is rare in Mexico (the DPD admits it but prefers hubiera).
si + pluperfect subjunctive + conditional: Si hubiera estudiado medicina, ahora sería médica.
si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional perfect: Si fuera más prudente, no habría tenido el accidente.
the conditional (si habría sabido) or the present subjunctive (si tenga). Si meaning "whether" can take the conditional: No sé si habría venido.
De ser así… (if that's the case); De haberlo sabido, te habría avisado (had I known…)
if it hadn't been for: De no haber sido por ti, me habría perdido.
Like ver: preveo, prevé, previsto, prevea, preveía; preterite preví, previó. Not "preveer".

cards.front: un acierto / un golpe de suerte / un imprevisto
cards.back: a good choice / a stroke of luck / something unexpected
thank goodness, just as well / otherwise (= B1's de otro modo)
at random / by chance
A short paid death notice: Con profundo pesar comunicamos el sensible fallecimiento de…; Descanse en paz.
A journalistic life story: news first (Falleció ayer…), then the life, then the legacy.
the wake (Spain el velatorio) / the burial (formal; el entierro)
mourning, its outward signs (estar de luto, vestirse de luto) / grief and the process of grieving (vivir el duelo)
In Catholic families, often nine days of prayers after a death, usually with the rosary; a Mass when it ends.
to pay tribute: La colonia le rendirá homenaje. rendir: rindo, rindió, rinda.
cemetery; el cementerio is general and usual in Spain
posthumous: una obra póstuma (published after the author's death), un homenaje póstumo
hube, hubiste, hubo… + participle, after apenas, no bien, en cuanto: Apenas hubo terminado, se fue. Modern: Apenas terminó, se fue.
la casa que construyera su abuelo = la casa que había construido su abuelo (not a subjunctive in meaning)
ellos preterite minus -ron + -re: tuvieron → tuviere; fueron → fuere; hubieron → hubiere
Old texts, some legal writing (El que incumpliere…) and set phrases (sea cual fuere; Adonde fueres, haz lo que vieres). Modern: sea cual sea.
no sooner, as soon as (literary): No bien llegó, empezó a llover.

cards.front: sea cual sea / sean cuales sean
cards.back: whatever it may be / whatever they may be: Sean cuales sean las razones, te apoyamos.
Affirmative opinion or certainty → indicative: Creo que es caro; Es evidente que consumimos demasiado. Negated → subjunctive: No creo que sea caro.

cards.front: ¿Crees que es caro? / ¿Crees que sea caro?
cards.back: Both are correct in questions; the subjunctive sounds more doubtful. Negative commands too: No pienses que es / sea fácil.
Subjunctive even for true facts: Es lógico que la ropa barata dure poco. Es injusto que ganen tan poco. Me parece normal que sea caro.

cards.front: Me parece que… vs me parece lógico que…
cards.back: Me parece que es caro (opinion: indicative). Me parece lógico que sea caro (value judgment: subjunctive).

cards.front: Value judgment with no particular subject
cards.back: Use the infinitive: Es absurdo gastar tanto. With a specific person: Es absurdo que gastes tanto.
No es que + subjunctive (the idea you reject), sino que + indicative (the real reason): No es que no me guste, sino que no tengo dinero.

cards.front: A que clause at the start
cards.back: Usually subjunctive: Que la ropa sea desechable me parece absurdo. El hecho de que takes either mood (the subjunctive is more frequent).

"The … thing": lo bueno, lo malo, lo difícil (always masculine singular). Lo bueno es que no cuesta mucho (+ indicative for a fact); Lo mejor es que lo devuelvas (+ subjunctive for what should happen).
"How …": No sabes lo caras que son (adjective agrees); Me sorprende lo rápido que cambia la moda (adverb invariable). Indicative after it.

cards.front: de segunda mano / la ropa de paca
cards.back: secondhand / in Mexico, used clothing that arrives in bales (pacas) and is sold at street markets (tianguis).
Present subjunctive (same time): Me molesta que grites. Perfect subjunctive (earlier): Me molesta que no me hayas avisado.
Imperfect subjunctive (same time): Me molestaba que gritaras. Pluperfect subjunctive (earlier): Me molestó que se hubieran comido mi pastel.

cards.front: Same subject with a feeling verb
cards.back: Infinitive: No soporto llegar tarde (I'm late). No soporto que llegues tarde (you're late).
Like gustar; the verb agrees with the person: Me cae bien tu hermana; Me caen bien tus amigos. Caer gordo (colloquial, very common in Mexico) is stronger, and gordo agrees: me cae gorda.
Work like gustar: Me sentó mal que no me invitaran. Me hizo gracia que lo notaras. Me fastidia que dejen la luz prendida.
Es tranquilo (his character). Hoy está insoportable (his behavior now). Es ordenada / Su cuarto está ordenado.

cards.front: es de los que / es de las que
cards.back: + indicative, usually plural: Es de las que nunca llegan a tiempo (DPD prefers the plural; singular admitted). Not soy de los que pienso → soy de los que piensan.
To get in a bad mood (informal), partner of B1's estar de malas: Se pone de malas cuando no hay café.
An obstacle you assert as fact: Aunque tengo vértigo, voy a subir.
A possibility, or a fact conceded as unimportant: Aunque llueva, vamos a subir. Aunque sea peligroso, me encanta.
Imaginary now: Aunque me pagaran, no haría paracaidismo. Imaginary past: Aunque hubiera llovido, habríamos subido.

cards.front: por más que / por mucho que / por poco que
cards.back: No matter how much / however little; usually + subjunctive (Por más que lo intente…), indicative for a known fact (Por más que lo intento, no me sale).
No matter how + adjective; usually + subjunctive; the adjective agrees: Por muy cansada que estuviera, nunca se quitaba el arnés.
pese a = formal a pesar de (+ noun, infinitive or que clause). si bien = although, formal and written, + indicative: Si bien el riesgo existe, es bajo.
aun cuando (formal): + subjunctive = even if, + indicative = even though. y eso que (spoken) + indicative, after the main clause: No se cansó, y eso que subió cinco horas.
aun = even (aun así, aun cuando, aun sabiéndolo). aún = still, yet (Aún no llegan).
now → future (Estará en el aeropuerto); recent past → future perfect (Habrá perdido la conexión); past → conditional (Serían las tres); before a past moment → conditional perfect (Ya habría salido).
habré, habrás, habrá, habremos, habrán + participle: habrá perdido, se habrá quedado dormida.
I wonder what's happened. / I wonder why he didn't come.
Debe de estar cansada (a guess); Debes llamar (an obligation). Deber alone for a guess (Debe estar cansada) is accepted by the Nueva gramática; avoid deber de for obligation.
lo más probable es que, es probable que, es posible que, puede que: Lo más probable es que llegue mañana.
seguramente, a lo mejor, capaz que (usually; colloquial in much of Latin America), Spain's colloquial igual: A lo mejor perdió la conexión.
Either mood before the verb: Quizás llega / llegue en la noche.
Supongo que + indicative (I suppose); suponiendo que + subjunctive (assuming that): Suponiendo que lleguemos a las diez…
Será muy bonito, pero está carísimo = It may be beautiful, but it's very expensive.
por lo general, suele, tiende a, en muchos casos, la mayoría de, no todos, hay quien, se dice que.
Either mood: Hay quien piensa que… (real people) / Hay quien piense que… (vaguer). Plural: hay quienes piensan.

cards.front: la mayoría de + plural noun + verb
cards.back: Singular or plural verb: La mayoría de los mexicanos vive / viven en ciudades.

cards.front: Answering a stereotype in three steps
cards.back: 1 concede (si bien es cierto que…), 2 limit (no es que + subjunctive, sino que…), 3 counterexample or sourced, dated fact (según el INEGI, en 2020…).
False friend: a commonplace, a cliché. "Topic" = el tema.
21% of the population lived in localities of fewer than 2,500 inhabitants; so about four in five lived in larger ones.
As a claim, not a fact: Se dice que…, Hay quien piensa que…; prefer people's own names for themselves; talk about diversity.
To tend to; stem changer like entender: tiendo, tiende, tienden. Los jóvenes tienden a mudarse a las ciudades.
Serían las cinco cuando… (past); Ya habrá visto las noticias (recent past); Estará preocupadísima (now).
"No se muevan." → Nos pidieron que no nos moviéramos (imperfect subjunctive after a past request).
Llamaron al 911 → Se recibió una llamada al 911. Nos encontraron → El grupo fue localizado. Nadie salió herido → No se reportaron heridos.
Feelings, guesses and the first person; it keeps times (14:30 horas), numbers and actions, with se and the ser passive.

cards.front: la insolación vs el golpe de calor
cards.back: insolación = sunstroke (from the sun: Le dio una insolación); golpe de calor = heatstroke in general.
A complex of seven canyons in the Sierra Tarahumara, Chihuahua (Meteored, 2025); rainy season June to September.
911, in service since October 2016 (rolled out state by state). Before a trip: Protección Civil guidance and the forecast.

cards.front: el relámpago, el rayo, el trueno
cards.back: the flash of lightning / the bolt that strikes / the thunder.
No commas = picks out which (Los inventores que patentaron…: only those). Commas = adds information (Los inventores, que patentaron…, se hicieron ricos: all of them).

cards.front: el cual, la cual, los cuales, las cuales
cards.back: Agrees with its antecedent. After prepositions (preferred after long ones: gracias al cual, frente a la cual) and, formally, after a comma. Never alone in a restrictive clause: el invento que cambió…

cards.front: el que or el cual after a preposition?
cards.back: After a, con, de, en, por: both (en el que / en el cual). After frente a, gracias a, a pesar de, según, durante: usually el cual.
Both refer to a whole idea after a comma: Llegó tarde, lo que / lo cual me molestó. Only lo que means "what": No entiendo lo que dices.
People only: after a preposition (con quien), after a comma, or as "whoever" (Quien lo sepa…). Not in a restrictive clause without a preposition: la mujer que inventó.
whose: agrees with the thing possessed: el inventor cuyas ideas…; no article after it; preposition before it: en cuyo laboratorio. Formal; spoken que su is nonstandard.
¿De quién…? (¿De quién es esta idea?) Cuyo is only a relative.

cards.front: donde, adonde, como, cuando as relatives
cards.back: la ciudad donde nació; el país adonde emigró (movement); la forma como funciona; en 1876, cuando…
Known antecedent: indicative (Tengo un colega que trabaja…). Unknown or nonexistent: subjunctive (Buscan a alguien que sepa…). After a superlative: either (que se ha hecho / que se haya hecho).
light bulb (Mexico and several other countries; Spain la bombilla); also focus.
to patent, the patent: Edison obtuvo en 1880 la patente de un foco incandescente.
Since, as: always before the main clause, indicative: Como subió la renta, nos mudamos. (After it, use porque: Nos mudamos porque subió la renta.)
debido a que + clause (formal): debido a que no tenía permisos; debido a / a causa de + noun: debido a la lluvia.

cards.front: gracias a (que) vs por culpa de
cards.back: gracias a: a cause with a good result; por culpa de: a bad result. Gracias a with a bad result is ironic.
Rejected cause in the subjunctive, real cause in the indicative: Se fue no porque quisiera, sino porque no podía pagar.
así que, por eso (everyday) → de modo que (neutral) → por lo tanto, en consecuencia (written) → por ende, así pues (formal).
hence, which is why: usually + subjunctive: Las rentas suben; de ahí que mucha gente se mude.
tan + adjective or adverb (tan caro que); tanto/a/os/as + noun (tantos departamentos que); verb + tanto que (cambió tanto que).
Usually a poor outlying district, not a well-off suburb. A planned housing development in Mexico: el fraccionamiento.
to become more expensive: se encarece, se encarecen; subjunctive se encarezca (c → zc like conocer).

cards.front: Purpose: same subject vs different subject
cards.back: para / a fin de / con el fin de + infinitive (same subject); para que / a fin de que / con el fin de que + subjunctive (different subject). A fin de and con el fin de are formal.

cards.front: no vaya a ser que / no sea que
cards.back: in case, so that… doesn't happen: + subjunctive, usually after the main clause: Lleva la receta, no vaya a ser que te la pidan.
once: + subjunctive for the future (Una vez que te den de alta…), + indicative for the past or a habit (Una vez que me dieron de alta…).
as, as gradually: two things changing together; subjunctive about the future: A medida que baje la inflamación, podrás doblar la rodilla.
whenever: indicative for a habit, subjunctive for the future. Siempre que + subjunctive can also mean "as long as".
desde que (since) + indicative for a real starting point: Desde que empecé…; antes de que always + subjunctive, even in the past: antes de que entrara.
when, on doing: Al salir del quirófano, me sentía mareado.
An extra (expletive) no that doesn't make it negative: No te vas hasta que no te baje la fiebre = hasta que te baje. Recognize it; you never need it.
as soon as: Nada más llegar, me llamó. In Mexico: En cuanto llegó, me llamó.

cards.front: dar de alta / dar de baja
cards.back: dar de alta: to discharge (from a hospital): Me dieron de alta. dar de baja: to cancel, to take off a list.
to prevent; like venir: prevengo, previne, prevendré, prevenga, previniendo; tú command prevén.
siempre y cuando, siempre que, con tal (de) que, a condición de que + subjunctive (as long as, provided that, on condition that).
a no ser que, a menos que, salvo que + subjunctive (unless). Excepto que + subjunctive = unless; + indicative = except that.

cards.front: en caso de que / en el supuesto de que
cards.back: in case, in the event that + subjunctive; en el supuesto de que is formal (contracts, laws).
just in case: + indicative (por si llueve) or imperfect subjunctive (por si lloviera); never the present subjunctive.
Como no pagues, te demandan = if (a warning). Como no pagaste, te demandaron = since (a cause).
De seguir así, perderán el juicio = Si siguen así… Past: De haberlo sabido, no habría firmado.
After a past or conditional verb: imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive: Me dijo que firmaría siempre y cuando le pagaran.
A lawsuit (juicio de amparo) that protects a person against an act of an authority that violates his or her rights; Constitution, articles 103 and 107.
A notario público is a lawyer appointed after an internship and an exam; much more than a US notary public.
prosecutor (la fiscal); the office is la fiscalía; the Constitution says el Ministerio Público, and people often say el ministerio público or el MP.
título, capítulo, artículo, párrafo, fracción (I, II, III), inciso (a, b, c), artículos transitorios.
An obligation, like "shall": El condómino pagará la cuota. Podrá = may (permission); queda prohibido / se prohíbe = is forbidden.
fuere, hiciere, hubiere, infringiere: read them as present subjunctives (sea, haga, haya, infrinja), or after si as a present indicative. Recognize; don't produce.
to come into force / to repeal: El reglamento entra en vigor mañana y deroga el anterior.
calendar days vs business days.
Find the verb; everything before it is the subject: La falta de pago de dos cuotas dará lugar a… (subject: la falta de pago).
Ley Federal de Protección al Consumidor (DOF, December 24, 1992), applied by Profeco. A warranty, when offered, lasts at least 90 days from delivery (art. 77).
Argentina, 1887–1971: half of the 1947 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine (a pituitary hormone and sugar metabolism).
Born in Paris 1906, died in Buenos Aires 1987: the whole 1970 Nobel Prize in Chemistry (sugar nucleotides).
Mexico, 1925–2004: synthesized norethisterone at Syntex on October 15, 1951, as a chemistry student.
Mexico, 1917–1965: Mexican patent (1940) for a color television system; presented in Mexico as its creator, though others showed color TV earlier.
Mexico City, 1943–2020: 1974 ozone study with Rowland; shared the 1995 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Rowland and Crutzen.
Born 1952, Chilpancingo: flew on Atlantis (STS-61-B), November 26 to December 3, 1985; first Mexican on a NASA space mission.
se le considera, se le atribuye, suele presentarse como, según…: keep the source's qualifier and say who makes the claim.
The prize: el Premio Nobel de Química (the press also writes el premio Nobel). A laureate, lowercase: Molina es premio nobel.

cards.front: Reported speech: present subjunctive after a past verb
cards.back: "Quiero que vengas" → Dijo que quería que fuera (imperfect subjunctive; -se also correct: fuese).
"No creo que lo hayan visto" → Dijo que no creía que lo hubieran visto (pluperfect subjunctive).
"Habremos terminado" → Dijo que habrían terminado (conditional perfect).
"Ojalá llueva" → Dijo que ojalá lloviera.

cards.front: What never shifts in reported speech
cards.back: The imperfect, pluperfect, conditional, conditional perfect and the imperfect and pluperfect subjunctive. A past condition stays as it is.
Me pidió que la llame mañana (still ahead) is normal; for a finished past situation use Me pidió que la llamara.
sostener, alegar, recalcar, subrayar, puntualizar, revelar, insinuar, replicar: Recalcó que no habría cambios.
pedir, sugerir, recomendar, aconsejar, suplicar, reprochar: Le suplicó que no lo publicara.
Advirtió que habría retrasos (warned that: fact). Advirtió que no saliéramos (warned us not to: instruction).
Insistió en que era inocente (insisted it was true). Insistió en que lo acompañara (insisted I go with him).
animar a + infinitive / a que + subjunctive; prometer + infinitive / que + conditional; amenazar con + infinitive.
¿Que si vienes mañana? = (I said) are you coming tomorrow? Spoken only; no accent on que.
ha sido aprobada, había sido cerrado, será inaugurado, habría sido evitado, que sea investigado. The participle agrees; sido never does.
The doer of a passive, introduced by por: fue escrito por una reportera (never de).
El caso está siendo investigado = is being investigated. News style: recognize it; say se está investigando in speech.
Se venden casas; se publicaron los resultados. The DPD says the verb agrees: not se vende casas.
Se detuvo a los sospechosos: singular verb + a. Never se detuvieron a.
Se vive bien aquí. Se trabaja mucho. Not with reflexive verbs: uno se levanta / la gente se levanta.

cards.front: Third-person plural for an unknown doer
cards.back: Dicen que va a llover. Me robaron la cartera. Never includes the speaker.
Participle: Detenido el presunto responsable. Present plural: Aprueban nueva ley. Noun: Aprobación de la reforma.
according to: según la policía, según fuentes oficiales; with pronouns, según yo / según tú (never según mí).
Crime and accident news in Mexico, often sensationalist. In Mexico una nota is also a news story.
Morbid curiosity / sensationalism: emotion and judgment instead of facts.
reflexive, reciprocal, se for le / les, pronominal verb, involvement, accidental, passive, impersonal.
se + me / te / le / nos / les + verb agreeing with the thing: Se me quemó el arroz; Se le cayeron los huevos.
Se comió todo el pastel; Me tomé un café. Adds completeness or enjoyment; the facts stay the same without it.
ir / irse (go / leave), llevar / llevarse (carry / take away, get along), quedar / quedarse (be located, fit / stay), poner / ponerse (put / put on, become).
Le di el libro → Se lo di. Never le lo.
Le di la receta a mi tía. A los niños les encanta. El mole lo hace mi abuela. Te lo dije a ti.
Se la voy a pedir / Voy a pedírsela; Pásamela; No se lo des.
Se los dije = se lo dije a ellos. Very common in speech; the DPD recommends se lo in careful speech.
Spain: A Juan le vi (le for a man as a direct object), accepted by the RAE. Latin America and this course: A Juan lo vi.
I think, it seems to me: Se me hace que va a llover. Takes the indicative.
el comal (griddle), el molcajete (stone mortar), el metate (grinding stone), el nixtamal (lime-treated corn), la masa (dough).
2010: traditional Mexican cuisine, with the "paradigm of Michoacán", joined UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
Llevo un año entrenando (I've been training for a year). Negative: Llevo dos meses sin correr.
Sigue lloviendo (it's still raining). Sigo sin entender (I still don't understand).
Voy mejorando (gradually). Vengo notándolo (for a while, up to now). Anda diciendo que… (going around saying, often critical).
ponerse a (start), echarse a reír / llorar / correr (burst out), dejar de (stop), volver a (again).
acabar / terminar + gerund (Acabé cambiando de entrenador); acabar por + infinitive (Acabó por aceptar).
Llegué a correr 20 km (went so far as, managed). No alcancé a estirar (didn't manage to in time; Latin America).
Mexico and some other Latin American countries: about to (El camión está por salir). Everywhere also still to be done (La cocina está por limpiar), the sense used in Spain.
Tengo pensado inscribirme (I'm planning to). Tengo escritas tres páginas (participle agrees).
Lo sigo intentando / Sigo intentándolo. Never between the two verbs.
la carrera = race; la constancia = perseverance; el calentamiento = warm-up.
A profile: a portrait built from an interview, mixing description, summary and a few quotations.
Recuerda que fue su primer referente; les aconseja que no esperen. Nothing shifts after a present reporting verb.
What only that person could say, in her own voice. Plain facts are reported, not quoted.
Every reporting verb interprets: insinúa, reprocha or alega where she explica is a quiet distortion.
Inside quotation marks, her words; cuts marked […] must not change the meaning; corrections are public.
For print the RAE recommends « » first; Mexican media mostly use " ". The period goes after the closing mark: …respeto".
role model, benchmark: Fue mi primer referente (usually masculine even for a woman).
science communicator; B1's la divulgación is the activity.
vocation, calling: Descubrió su vocación a los quince años.
Source, date, original context, reverse image search, confirmation by other reliable sources. Verdict: verdadero, engañoso or falso.
Spain's everyday word for a hoax or false story; Mexico usually says noticia falsa or fake news.
supuestamente, al parecer, según…, presunto; the news conditional (habría sido creado) for recognition.
Se trata de un montaje. La imagen fue tomada en 2017. Se consultó a dos expertos.
En una versión anterior de esta nota se afirmaba que…; el dato fue corregido.
Urgency (¡Compártelo ya!), no source, capital letters, a screenshot instead of a link, built to make you angry or afraid.
verifiqué (c → qu); se viralizó (keeps se).
reliable, trustworthy; confiable is very common in Latin America.
Mexican collaborative fact-checking project (Animal Político, AJ+ Español, Pop-Up Newsroom, about 90 partners) for the July 1, 2018 election.
A connector (porque, aunque) joins two clauses; a discourse marker (de hecho, por cierto) tells the listener how to take what follows. Markers can move and go between commas.
or rather: corrects what you just said. El lunes, mejor dicho, el martes.
in other words: restates an idea more plainly (like es decir; a little formal).
in fact: backs up what was said with a fact, often a stronger one. Son importantes. De hecho, son lo primero que reviso.
actually, really: sets reality against an appearance. Parece fácil, pero en realidad no lo es. (actualmente = currently)
rather: swaps in a more exact word. No es malo; es más bien caro.

cards.front: además → es más → encima / para colmo
cards.back: From neutral to exasperated: es más adds a stronger point; encima and para colmo (colloquial) pile up complaints.
by the way: opens a side remark. A propósito can do the same job.
after all: gives the reason that settles the matter.

cards.front: de todos modos / en cualquier caso
cards.back: anyway / in any case: what came before doesn't change the conclusion. Also de todas formas, de todas maneras.
oh well, well anyway; in short: wraps up, often with resignation. Rarely "finally" today (por último, finalmente).
so in the end (colloquial): introduces the outcome of a story. Total, que no me contrataron.
Cohesion: sentences visibly linked (connectors, markers, pronouns). Coherence: the ideas make sense in that order.
to apply for a vacancy (Mexico); Spain presentarse a un puesto. Aplicar a is a common calque in speech.
un puesto de planta = permanent position with benefits; un trabajador independiente = freelancer.
-ción, -sión, -dad, -ura, -anza, -eza: feminine. -miento, -aje: masculine. El análisis is masculine too.
la mejora (not mejoración).
el análisis (plural los análisis).

cards.front: nominal style: how to unpack it
cards.back: Find the nouns that hide verbs, ask who does each action, rebuild with verbs. La reducción del consumo… → consumieron menos…
lo ocurrido (what happened), lo dicho (what was said), lo expuesto (what has been set out).
el fumar, el ir y venir: formal or literary; recognize it.
llevar a cabo un estudio, realizar un análisis, efectuar una medición, tomar una decisión, dar una explicación.
Se analizaron 300 muestras. Se observó que… Se recomienda…
Los datos sugieren que… Los resultados parecen indicar que… Esto podría deberse a…
Correlation doesn't imply causation. Only an experiment (un ensayo clínico, with un placebo) can test a cause.
Both can mean evidence: No hay pruebas de que… La evidencia científica (very common in Latin America; some style guides prefer pruebas).
peer review: other experts check un artículo científico before publication.
Singular or plural: opina / opinan (DPD: both; plural generally more frequent). Plural with an adjective: están satisfechos.
Percentages take an article: el for a precise figure, un for an approximate or new one. RAE: a space before % (el 40 %).
la mitad, un tercio, dos tercios, la cuarta parte, tres de cada diez (plural verb), uno de cada cinco (singular verb).
La cifra pasó del 7 % al 14 %.
El desempleo aumentó en dos puntos.
20 % → 25 %: cinco puntos porcentuales, which is un 25 % more.
to double, to triple (third person: se duplicó). Reducirse a la mitad = to halve.
incrementar + object (incrementó el presupuesto); for something rising by itself, incrementarse or aumentar.

cards.front: frente a, en comparación con, respecto a, mientras que
cards.back: against, compared with, compared to / regarding, whereas.
DPD: group digits with a space (126 014 024); decimal point or comma by country. Mexico: 3.6; Spain: 3,6.
126 014 024 inhabitants; median age 29 (22 in 2000); 3.6 occupants per home (4.4 in 2000). Source: INEGI.
asunto; saludo with a colon; motivo (Me dirijo a usted para…); datos; opinión; petición (Le agradecería que + imperfect subjunctive); despedida (Quedo a su disposición… Atentamente).
The level of formality you keep throughout: usted, formal words (descender, el incremento), neutral markers, formal greeting and closing.

cards.front: estar de acuerdo en que / con que
cards.back: + indicative: accepting a fact (en que el agua es el problema). + subjunctive: approving a proposal (con que se cobre más). Both prepositions occur with both meanings. Negative: subjunctive usual.
+ indicative, then pero: Tienes razón en que las fugas son un problema, pero…
+ subjunctive: refutes a conclusion. …eso no quiere decir que haya funcionado.
No es que + subjunctive, es que + indicative: No es que sean malas, es que no resuelven nada.
Yo propondría que / Sería conveniente que / Lo ideal sería que + imperfect subjunctive; Habría que + infinitive; ¿Y si + imperfect subjunctive?
Sum up the other side; concede (Es cierto que…); rebut (Sin embargo, eso no quiere decir que…); propose (Yo propondría que…).
viable; feasible; effective (plural eficaces). Eficaz = achieves its effect; eficiente = without waste.

cards.front: a corto plazo / a largo plazo
cards.back: in the short term / in the long term.
subsidy (often lowers a price) / grant to an organization or project; Mexican usage often says subsidio for both.
to raise awareness (Mexico, much of Latin America); Spain concienciar. Noun: la concientización.
Prepared: a problem with a set of proposals; you evaluate them, choose and defend, then discuss with the examiner (about 6–7 minutes per the 2014 guide).
Find the thesis, mark the steps, close the source, write from notes, check the meaning.
to put in your own words: change structure, order, voice and words; still cite the source.
A direct quotation, short, exact, with a reporting verb and a reference: (Ferrer, 2019, p. 45).
RAE: angle quotes « » first in printed texts; in Mexico double quotes " " are more common. Be consistent.

cards.front: la nota al pie / la bibliografía
cards.back: footnote (Chicago puts the full reference there) / the list of sources at the end.
APA, Chicago or your institution's style: pick one and use it everywhere.
En este trabajo analizamos… / En este trabajo se analizan… Pick one; avoid yo.
afirma, señala, sostiene, advierte que + indicative; propone que + subjunctive.
Same sentences with synonyms and no reference = plagiarism. New structure + reference = paraphrase.

cards.front: un congreso / una conferencia / una ponencia
cards.back: conference (event) / a single lecture / a talk or paper given at a conference.
presenter at a conference (la ponente); Latin America also el expositor.
Mi ponencia tiene tres partes… Paso ahora a… Como decía… Abro un paréntesis… Recapitulando… Para concluir… Quedo atenta a sus preguntas.
to present, set out (like poner): expongo, expuse, expuesto, expón, expondré.
Thanks, a compliment to the others, the people behind the work, a dedication, thanks again: under a minute.
q = que, xq = porque, tb = también, c/ = con, s/ = sin, ej. = por ejemplo, aprox., s. XX, → ↑ ↓.
Day / month / year: 4/9/1969 = September 4, 1969.
A long monologue such as a lecture or speech, heard twice, with questions on main ideas and details (2014 guide).
el abrelatas, el sacacorchos, el paraguas, el rascacielos: masculine, plural unchanged (los abrelatas), one stress on the noun part.
the opposite, undoing: hacer → deshacer, conectar → desconectar, armar → desarmar
not: útil → inútil, posible → imposible (im- before p, b), legal → ilegal, regular → irregular (i- before l, r; r doubled)
again (rehacer), before (precalentar), too much (sobrecargar), together (coautor), self (autoestima)
adjectives: lavable (can be washed), ruidoso (full of noise), creativo (tending to create)
jobs and containers: el zapatero, el salero, la cafetera, el llavero; shops: la zapatería, la ferretería
a blow or a sudden act: el portazo (la puerta), el frenazo, el martillazo, el flechazo (love at first sight); informally "great": un golazo
-ito (casita), -cito (cafecito, camioncito), -ecito (panecito; Mexico also pancito). Spelling: poco → poquito, amigo → amiguito.
affection (mi abuelita), politeness (un momentito), intensity (cerquita, rapidito). Very frequent in Mexico.
right now, in a moment, a little while ago, or a polite "later": context and tone decide.
-ón (el cucharón, la casona; llorón, mandón), -ote (grandote, la palabrota), -azo (el perrazo)
el desarmador (destornillador), el trapeador (la fregona), la cubeta (el cubo), el destapador (el abrebotellas), el lavatrastes: kitchen sink
purpose (para ver aves), destination (para el mirador), deadline (para el viernes), opinion (para mí), comparison (para ser enero), recipient (para ti), employer (para el gobierno)
cause (por la lluvia), through or along (por la sierra), rough place or time (por aquí, por la tarde), means (por teléfono), exchange (por 90 pesos), duration, agent of the passive, on behalf of
still to be done: Quedan tres kilómetros por recorrer. In much of Latin America estar por = to be about to: Está por llover.
to be in the mood for: No estoy para bromas. (Also "about to"; Mexico prefers estar por.)
for someone's sake, because of them / for an employer, or meant for them
why (the cause) / what for (the purpose)
just in case; almost (with the present for a past near-miss: Por poco me caigo)
par excellence, the quintessential: el paisaje yucateco por excelencia

cards.front: a orillas de, en lo alto de, al pie de, en el fondo de
cards.back: on the shores of, at the top of, at the foot of, at the bottom of
Mexico's first national park (1917, under Venustiano Carranza): a conifer forest on the edge of Mexico City.
Biosphere reserve in Quintana Roo; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987: forests, mangroves, marshes and part of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef.
a natural sinkhole with water, common in the Yucatán Peninsula; the axolotl, endemic to the Valley of Mexico
80 minutes, 2 tasks of 150–180 words: a letter or e-mail from notes on a recording; an opinion piece chosen from two options (an article commenting on a graph, or a blog article or a review).
read and underline every point → choose the register → outline → draft → edit → count the words
la introducción (topic and tesis), el desarrollo (one main idea per paragraph, with ideas secundarias), la conclusión (sums up or proposes; no new argument)
Estimados señores: / Me dirijo a ustedes en relación con… / Quedo a la espera de su respuesta. / Atentamente,
use a sinónimo (la medida, la iniciativa), a pronoun, or a noun (la construcción del puente)
Never between a subject and its verb: La propuesta del ayuntamiento me parece excelente.
semicolon: in lists whose items contain commas, and between linked sentences, often before a connector: …; sin embargo, …
colon: after a letter's greeting (then a capital), before lists, examples and explanations (then usually lowercase)
days, months, languages and nationalities (el lunes, septiembre, el español, mexicano); titles capitalize only the first word: Cien años de soledad
because / why / the reason
reading 70 min (4 tasks, 36 items); listening 40 min (5 tasks, 30 items, each recording twice); writing 80 min (2 tasks); speaking 20 min after 20 to prepare (3 tasks)
100 points in two groups: reading + writing, listening + speaking. At least 30 of 50 in each group for Apto; no compensation between groups.

cards.front: DELE B2: marking writing and speaking
cards.back: 0–3 scales (band 2 = B2); holistic 40%, analytic 60%. Writing: adecuación, coherencia, corrección, alcance. Speaking: coherencia, fluidez, corrección, alcance.
Texts from many varieties. In answers, any educated Hispanic norm is accepted if used consistently.
In reading and listening a wrong answer costs nothing: answer every item.
Main verb present, future, perfect or command → present (same time or later) or perfect subjunctive (before). Main verb past or conditional → imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive.
Si hubiera salido antes, no habría (hubiera) perdido el vuelo. Si hubiera estudiado medicina, ahora sería médica. De haberlo sabido, te habría avisado.
present → imperfect; preterite or perfect → pluperfect; future → conditional; future perfect → conditional perfect; command → imperfect subjunctive
vos hablás, comés, vivís; tenés, podés (no stem change); sos, vas, has
hablá, comé, viví; vení, decí, poné; sentate, fijate, decime; andá (for ir)

cards.front: What stays the same with vos
cards.back: the preterite (vos hablaste), the object pronoun te, the possessive tu; after prepositions: para vos, con vos

cards.front: el tuteo, el voseo, el ustedeo
cards.back: using tú; using vos and its verb forms; using usted for closeness (Costa Rica, parts of Colombia)
the pronoun tú with voseo endings: ¿Tú sabís?, ¿Cómo estái?
hey (Argentina, Uruguay); you know?, see? (a tag in the Río de la Plata)
all good, great, also hello or thanks (Costa Rica); a Costa Rican (informal)
the slang of Buenos Aires; the infusion of yerba mate, and the gourd it's drunk from
A problem and a card of proposals: weigh pros and cons, say which you prefer and why, then discuss with the examiner (6–7 min).
A photo of an imagined situation: describe, imagine, hypothesize (5–6 min). Al fondo…, supongo que…, si yo estuviera…
A short conversation about survey results or news (3–4 min): react, explain, give an example, ask back.
about 10 for task 1, 8 for task 2, 2 to review; notas de apoyo in key words, or a mapa conceptual
Bueno…, A ver…, ¿Cómo lo diría?; Lo que quiero decir es que…, Mejor dicho…, O sea…

cards.front: la soltura, la pausa, la vacilación
cards.back: ease in speaking (fluency), a pause, hesitation: pauses are normal; fill them with Spanish (bueno, a ver), not silence or English
